title: Notice of Intent to Award Sole Source Bridge Contract
description: This is not a request for quote/proposal. This notice is issued pursuant to FAR 5.201(b), Washington Headquarters Services, on behalf of the Office of the Under Secretary of War for the Office of the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security (OUSW(I&S)). The purpose of this notice is to award a short-term, sole source bridge extension to the incumbent contractor Quality Systems Management Inc. (QSMI), [CAGE Code: 080T3; 7700 Little River Turnpike Suite 202, Annandale, VA 22003-2427]. The Contractor is currently performing services under task order HQ0034-21-F-0418, with services concluding on December 13, 2026. The Government intends to extend the contract period of performance (POP) to ensure continuity of services while the Government works to award a competitive long-term, follow-on contract. WHS/AD anticipates award of the follow-on contract by September 11, 2027. Therefore, a nine-month bridge extension will be required to secure continued contractor support. The bridge extension has a total estimated value of $741,318.44 using fiscal year (FY) 2027 Operations & Maintenance (O&M) Funds. The POP for the bridge extension is from December 11, 2026, to September 10, 2027. The anticipated award will be made under the authority of General Services Administration Acquisition Regulation (GSAR) class deviation, specifically within GSAR subpart 538.71.

title: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services (APS) Department of the Army
description: *** 11/16/2026: AMENDMENT 07 ISSUED - SEE SUMMARY OF AMENDMENT AT BOTTOM OF POSTING*** ***SUMMARY ONLY - SEE ATTACHED COMBINED SYNOPSIS/SOLICITATION DOCUMENT FOR FULL DETAIL*** APS _ Combined Synopsis/Solicitation Brief: Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Commercial Items Agile Professional Services ("APS�) Department of the Army Project Name: Agile Professional Services ("APS") Solicitation Number: W900KK-26-R-A023 NAICS Code: 541990 (All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services) Set-Aside: Total Small Business Set-Aside Contract Type: Labor Hours/T&M 1. General Information This combined synopsis/solicitation is issued by Army Contracting Command - APG - Orlando Division to procure Agile Professional Services ("APS"). The acquisition is structured to support critical technical and professional operations under a flexible framework, to be proposed and developed by the successful offeror. Key acquisition parameters include: � Set-Aside Status: 100% Total Small Business Set-Aside. � Small Business Size Standard: $19.5M, or as defined by SBA regulations. � Primary NAICS Classification: 541990 � All Other Professional, Scientific, and Technical Services. � Contract Vehicle Type: Labor Hours/T&M 2. Solicitation Details This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. This combined synopsis/solicitation is prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Subpart 12.6, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular FAC 2025-06, effective August 27, 2025.and DFARS Publication Notice (DPN) July 2, 2026. As described in the attached FAR 52.212-2, The Army will adopt aspects of FAR Part 15 evaluation procedures. Considering the novel, and commercial, nature of these services this is deemed necessary to balance fairness, transparency, and competition with the interests of expediency and flexibility 3. Description of Requirement CPE ST3 has a need for Agile Professional Services (APS) support services to provide the organization with the ability to augment its Military and Government Civilian workforce in order to execute its mission. The services will be limited to providing professional support services, under a Performance Based Services model, to CPE ST3 and CPE ST3 customers for limited requirements which are related to CPE ST3�s mission. Since its inception, CPE ST3 has relied on contractor support to conduct its mission in all phases of life cycle management due to insufficient personnel within the organization to successfully perform the required services. This model of a Government footprint with a scalable contractor workforce has enabled CPE ST3 to be very flexible and agile in its mission to support the changing needs of the Army. The services to be performed will include related activities in support of all aspects of providing responsive integrated and interoperable infrastructure for simulation, training, testing, and threat solutions. APS support services are required for effective, efficient, and responsive full lifecycle management of efforts to include, but not limited to: vision statements and doctrine, development of architectures, program support (e.g., acquisition and budget planning, business and financial programming and execution, modeling, simulation, simulator, training device, and instrumentation development, documentation, fielding and execution, system analysis and integration, integrated logistics support, strategic planning, contingency and mission support, security cooperation/international relations, program oversight, independent verification validation and test evaluation, prototype development, sustainment and operations, and analysis of emerging technologies support), and subject matter experts on military tactics, techniques, and procedures. Potential areas of growth are envisioned but not limited to be in the areas of Cyber and Information Warfare, Robotics, Unmanned Vehicles, Home Station Training, Multi-Sensory Simulation, Artificial Intelligence, Hypersonics, Directed Energy, Electronic Warfare, Autonomous Systems, Multi-Domain Integration, Target and Threat Systems, Environment Modeling, Human Performance Training, Security Cooperation, Nuclear Engineering, and Medical Training. The critical performance requirement is the successful development and transition of CPE ST3 from a traditional, staffing-based support model to a task-based, outcome-driven Agile delivery framework that is to be developed by the Performer. Success will be measured by the contractor's ability to develop and iterate, through performance under the resultant contract, a framework that both provides the following, and is able to be replicated across future requirements. 4. Period of Performance / Performance Locations: Total Performance Period shall not exceed 66-months: Base Period � (15-Mar-27 to 14-Sep-27) Agile Development and Transition In Option Period 1 � (15-Sep-27 to 14-Sep-28) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 2 � (15-Sep-28 to 14-Sep-29) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 3 � (15-Sep-29 to 14-Sep-30) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 4 � (15-Sep-30 to 14-Sep-31) � Enterprise Performance Option Period 5 � (15-Sep-31 to 14-Mar-32) � Enterprise Performance and Transition Out Option Period 6 � (15-Mar-32 to 14-Sep-32) � Option to Extend the Term of Service under FAR 52.217-8 * Work will be performed at Government facilities, Contractor facilities, and Remote locations. Primary Government sites include Orlando, FL, and Redstone Arsenal, AL (including 24/7 operations). Additional Government sites include: Fort Campbell, KY; Fort Hood, TX; Fort Drum, NY; Fort Irwin, CA; Fort Polk, LA; Fort Rucker, AL; Fort Bragg, NC; Hohenfels, Germany; and Camp Humphreys, South Korea. 5. Applicable FAR Provisions/Provisions: See Attachment 7. The provisions and clauses apply to this acquisition and are incorporated by reference or full text as applicable. The full text of the FAR and DFARS clauses may be accessed electronically at https://www.acquisition.gov/. 6. Proposal Submission Instructions Phase II responses to this solicitation are due by 30 November 2026 / 10:00am (Eastern). Submission due dates for all subsequent Phases will be issued via Advisory Notifications / Invitations. a. Electronic Submission Requirement All proposals must be submitted electronically via the Department of Defense Secure Access File Exchange (DoD SAFE) application at https://safe.apps.mil . Hardcopy submissions or proposals sent directly via standard email will not be accepted. b. DoD SAFE Link Upon issuance of Phase II Notification / Invitation, the Government will be issuing each respective Offeror (2) DoD SAFE links. Links will be sent to the POC identified in the Phase I Cover Letter: DoD SAFE Link #1 - Pick Up - JIRA Data: Each Offeror will receive an email from DoD SAFE with a link in which to download all the JIRA Data and Instructions. DoD SAFE Link #2 - Drop Off - Phase II Proposal Submittal: Each Offeror will receive a secondary email from DoD SAFE with a link to upload all their respective documents for Phase II, including the final PowerPoint Presentation and their attendee list for Oral Presentations. Link Validity: Once the Government issues the pick-up and drop-off, each Offeror will receive automated emails from DoD SAFE containing the unique links and instructions. These links are valid for exactly 14 days from the date of receipt. WARNING: The Government will not be held responsible for late proposals resulting from an offeror's failure to submit a drop-off by the established deadline. c. Submission Protocol Upon receipt of the automated DoD SAFE email link: Click the link inside the automated email to access the secure upload portal. Upload all required solicitation attachments, ensuring they are named clearly.

title: RFP-797-FSS-04-0001-R3: 621II Medical Laboratory Testing & Analysis Services
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. Current contract holders do not need to complete sections below: GEOGRAPHIC COVERAGE Current Coverage: List the specific U.S. states, including Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington D.C., and U.S. territories in which you are currently providing or have provided services relative to this solicitation in the last two years. Enter Nationwide if currently/recently providing nationwide (i.e. domestic delivery) coverage. Proposed Coverage: Offerors may propose to provide service to individual states or nationwide. Respond to each question below regarding proposed coverage. For each choice selected, you must also check the box to verify your submission of the requested supporting documentation. Please note that qualifying supporting documentation means evidence of compliance with all federal, state and local license and certification in accordance with Statement of Work, Section II General Qualifications and Sub-Factor B.1 Organization sub-paragraph (a)(b) - Organizational and Professional Staff. title: Q301--Reference Laboratory Testing
description: NO PROPOSALS OR QUOTATIONS ARE REQUESTED AT THIS TIME. THIS PRE-SOLICITATION NOTICE IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THE FORMAL RFP WILL BE POSTED AT SAM.GOV UNDER THIS NOTICE NUMBER 36C24227R0003 ON OR ABOUT 10/07/2026. OFFERORS ARE ENCOURAGED TO MONITOR SAM.GOV FOR THE FORTHCOMING RFP AND SUPPORTING DOCUMENTATION. Brief Description of Services: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 2, on behalf of Veterans Integrated Service Network (VISN) 2 South, intends to issue an RFP - Requirements Contract for comprehensive Reference Laboratory and Esoteric Testing Services. The contract will serve the VA Medical Centers listed in Appendix A. The contractor must provide everything needed to perform all required reference and esoteric laboratory testing. This includes, but is not limited to: All personnel, labor, equipment, transportation, information technology, supplies, and supervision Routine and STAT pickup and transportation of specimens from multiple VA medical facilities to the contractor s laboratory Pre-analytic processing and preservation of samples Performance of laboratory analysis as specified in the contractor s test manual and relevant standards Timely electronic and hardcopy reporting of results to ordering VA facilities, with direct system interface to the VA VistA Laboratory Information System (LIS) Consultation regarding test selection, specimen collection, result interpretation, and specimen requirements Provision of all consumables for specimen collection, preservation, and transport Maintenance of all required certifications and accreditations Compliance with HIPAA and VA information security requirements A complete Statement of Work, with all details and requirements, will be included in the final solicitation. Locations of Service (Appendix A): James J. Peters VA Medical Center VA New Jersey Healthcare System VA Hudson Valley Healthcare System VA New York Harbor Healthcare System Northport VA Medical Center Set-Aside: Unrestricted, this is not Set-Aside. NAICS: 621511 Medical Laboratories

title: Q702--Santa Maria IOTA
description: Department of Veterans Affairs Veterans Health Administration Program Contracting Activity Central (PCAC) October 13, 2026 PRESOLICITATION NOTICE Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation Services in support of the Santa Maria, CA OPC 100% SDVOSB SET ASIDE This is a Pre-Solicitation Notice that the Veterans Health Administration (VHA) intends to solicit quotes to provide non-personal Initial Outfitting, Transition, and Activation (IOT&A) services for the Santa Maria Outpatient Clinic (OPC). This requirement supports VHA's mission by providing contractor support services to help bring the hospital into full planned operations that will provide health care services to Veterans. This will be a firm-fixed-price contract with an estimated Period of Performance of 31-months. VHA authorized a 28,656 net usable square foot (NUSF) outpatient clinic (OPC) lease project in Santa Maria, California. The project will support the parent facility, the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Greater Los Angeles Healthcare System. The new OPC will replace the existing clinic in Santa Maria, which currently contains 28,612 NUSF. The new clinic will be able to accommodate future workload, provide ample parking (200 spaces), and will adequately support all services in a modern, efficient space. The new clinic will provide all the services offered at the existing clinic, including Primary Care, Mental Health, Audiology, Eye Clinic, Dental, Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, Pathology and Blood Draw, Logistics, Telehealth, Business Office, Community Engagement and Reintegration, and Women's Health. This new facility is essential to accommodate the current demand of 6,634 Unique Santa Maria Veterans and the future potential demand of 7,500 Santa Maria catchment Enrollees The scope includes project support for planning, activating, outfitting, and transitioning the staff and Veterans/patients associated with the project. The scope of services includes Comprehensive Project Management, Comprehensive Interior Design, FF&E, and Space Planning Support; CONOPS and Transitioning Planning; Acquisition Support Services to include package development, Activation, Delivery, Relocation and Installation, Training, and Turnover and Post Occupancy Support for the identified project. This requirement will be set-aside 100% for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) using FAR Part 12 and 37. To be eligible for an SDVOSB set aside under VA s Veterans First Contracting Program, SDVOSBs must: be verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) as SDVOSB (see https://search.certifications.sba.gov/ for details) and meet the small business size standard for NAICS 541614. The solicitation is anticipated to be posted on Contract Opportunities for download on or about 30 October 2026. Potential offerors are advised that there may be truncated response time on the solicitation that will follow this Pre-Solicitation notice. Anticipated closing date of the solicitation will be 30 November 2026. Solicitation initial posting date and the closing date are subject to change as necessary. Any questions for this Pre-solicitation notice should be sent via e-mail to both Katherine.Johnson6@va.gov and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov. No telephone requests/questions will be accepted. This Pre-Solicitation notice does not constitute a request for proposals. P.O.C: Katherine.Johnson@va.gov, Contract Specialist and Kathleen.Klotzbach@va.gov, Contracting Officer

title: 8470-- Police Ballistic Vests
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 6, on behalf of the Richmond VA Medical Center (VAMC), is conducting market research and issuing this Sources Sought Notice to identify qualified vendors capable of providing police ballistic vests and related equipment. The required ballistic protection system must meet the following specifications to ensure reliable performance, compatibility, officer comfort, and mobility during routine law enforcement operations: Point Blank AXBIIIA Hi-Lite custom ballistic vests, including one vest for K-9 use. Ballistic vest carriers. Speed plates with a multi-curve shooter s cut, including one plate for K-9 use. Gen 3 slick carriers. National Institute of Justice (NIJ) Level IIIA protection capable of stopping common handgun threats, including 9mm and .44 Magnum ammunition. Comprehensive protection for the chest, sides, and back. Velcro straps or comparable quick-release features to facilitate rapid donning and removal during emergency situations. Multi-curve plates designed to improve fit, comfort, and mobility. Durable, breathable carrier materials to maximize comfort during extended wear. Documentation certifying compliance with NIJ Level IIIA standards. Products that meet all applicable specifications and performance requirements. Individual measurements for each wearer to ensure proper fit. Training on the proper use, care, and maintenance of the ballistic protection system, if required. Important Notice This notice is issued solely for market research and acquisition-planning purposes. PROGRAM/PROJECT OVERVIEW: The 11th Contracting Squadron (11 CONS), District of Washington, has a requirement to execute the design-build upgrades, repairs, and/or replacements to the deteriorated Electrical Switching Stations located at B18 and B168 on Joint Base Anacostia Bolling (JBAB) that includes developing a solution to establish a connection by high voltage electrical redundancy cable. The Government is evaluating the feasibility of executing these requirements via Progressive Design-Build (PDB) utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. This project summary establishes the operational requirements, technical baseline, and acquisition framework for the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) Other Transaction Authority (OTA) effort to modernize Joint Base Anacostia-Bolling�s (JBAB) primary electrical infrastructure. (PDB) via Other Transaction Authority (OTA) Primary Objective Engineer comprehensive design packages to repair, upgrade, and interconnect deteriorated electrical switching infrastructure Primary by Facility & Component ESS B18 (Switching Station Upgrade) � Full replacement of legacy switchgear with FR3 fluid, air-insulated switchgear (per latest UFC 3-550-01) � Life-cycle cost and High-efficiency interior LED lighting ESS B168 (Repair, Upgrade & Hardening) � Complete switchgear replacement mirroring ESS B168b using FR3 air-insulated switchgear (UFC 3-550-01) � Sustainable physical comm trunk lines � Relay-to-control panel comm wiring for ESS B18 and ESS B168 � Additional telemetry control panel integrated into ESS B4505 (sub-station to B18) to monitor sub-station power title: RFP-797-FSS-04-0001-R3: 621II Medical Laboratory Testing & Analysis Services
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. title: FY27 Scott AFB Air Show Narrator
description: Scott Air Force Base is in need of a Narrator for upcoming Air Show in June of 2027. The Contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, tools, materials, supervision, transportation, communications capability, and other items and services necessary to perform Airshow Narrator services for the 2027 Scott AFB Airshow, except for Government-furnished property and services specifically identified in this Performance Work Statement (PWS). The Contractor shall provide an experienced and currently qualified Airshow Narrator to support safe, professional, timely, and engaging presentation of the Airshow in accordance with AFMAN 10-1004, Conducting Air Force Open Houses; approved installation plans; the approved flying schedule; the applicable mishap/emergency-response plan; and local Scott AFB procedures. The Airshow Narrator shall narrate the airshow and keep spectators informed of ongoing and upcoming events, approved sponsor recognition, activities, entertainment, concessions, public service announcements, safety information, and other Government-approved messages. The Contractor shall coordinate directly with the Government-designated Airshow Director, Contracting Officer's Representative (COR), Air Operations Officer, Air Boss, Ground Boss, public affairs personnel, emergency-response agencies, performers, sound-support contractor, and other agencies designated by the Government. The Contractor shall not issue aviation-control instructions, direct emergency responders, make unapproved public statements, or modify Government-approved emergency language. The Contractor shall promptly communicate approved emergency, safety, weather, schedule, evacuation, shelter, accountability, and crowd-control messages when directed by the Government-designated responsible person or in accordance with the approved emergency plan. The Contractor shall attend, either in person or virtually, all required 2027 Scott AFB Airshow planning meetings with Scott AFB Airshow staff. At a minimum, the Contractor shall attend four monthly planning meetings, or fewer if coordinated with Scott AFB Airshow staff. The Contractor may be required to attend additional meetings and shall attend those meetings virtually unless otherwise directed by the Government. All required in-person meetings, designated site visits, travel, and associated expenses shall be included in the Contractor's price proposal, except for Government-furnished lodging and transportation identified in this PWS. The Airshow Narrator shall be on site for the Airshow rehearsal on 11 June 2027 and for the 2027 Scott AFB Airshow on 12 and 13 June 2027. Additionally, the Airshow Narrator shall be available on site during the week of the Airshow to support approved promotions, media engagements, planning meetings, performer coordination, sound checks, and other Airshow-related requirements as directed by the Government. Specific event times for all dates will be determined and provided by the Government. The Contractor shall provide all services described in this PWS at Scott AFB, provided weather, installation conditions, safety requirements, and operational requirements permit performance. Please reference the PWS attachement.

title: RFP-797-FSS-04-0001-R3: 621II Medical Laboratory Testing & Analysis Services
description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. title: Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) Renewal
description: INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Wharton Research Data Services products (WRDS) #SS-OFR-27-006 The Treasury Common Services Center (TCSC), on behalf of the Office of Financial Research (OFR) and the Financial Stability Oversight Council (FSOC), intends to contract with Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania, 3451 Walnut St Ste 440A, Philadelphia, PA 19104-6205, on a sole source basis. There is no competitive vendor or regulatory agency that provides these datasets. The proposed Contractor developed and owns the propriety and patented hardware, software and algorithms that are used in these products and support the services specifically required for this acquisition; thereby, the proposed source has the sole unique technical and other resources required for this acquisition. Pursuant to its mandate, the OFR/FSOC has a need for access to business, financial, economic, and marketing data through a self-managed service with centralized access; a high volume of cross-disciplinary data; and flexibility of delivery including computing cloud access. With this data, the OFR/FSOC also requires technical and research technical, and research specialists available for online assistance and orientation toward academic research information furnished on a platform which consolidates access to major datasets and databases used by academia, regulatory agencies, and commercial entities with financial market and economic information requirements to meet these needs, the OFR/FSOC is pursuing Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) access. WRDS consolidates access through one platform to commonly accessed financial data sets such as FactSet Revere, S&P CUSIP, Hedge Fund Research, and others. WRDS is the only known platform which creates single point access to commercial datasets such as CUSIP, MF Links, CRSP and other baseline financial data. This expedites research and crisis response as multiple portals need not be consulted to perform the necessary due diligence. OFR needs to purchase WRDS to obtain regulatory and original source financial data and integrate it with information from baseline financial commercial datasets in order to effectively fulfill its mission of anticipating systemic threats to the financial system and publishing the studies found in its Financial Monitor. Much of the source data is not readily obtainable from other sources in its original form nor from a single point of access. The source data and ease of access enable the OFR to respond to critical emergent analytical requests more readily within the financial services sector. Integrating data from different sources and possessing a single point of access for it allows for new insights that may be critical in understanding fast-moving market developments during times of crisis. Whilst regulatory data collections implicitly define data standards these implicit standards do not always envision the benefits of integration with other (commercial) sources. These challenges have a significant impact on the ability to quickly perform research and analysis across multiple datasets. The OFR and FSOC will use the proposed contractor�s brand name product for the continuing mission to deliver an annual assessment of the state of the U.S. financial system, as required by the Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform and Consumer Protection Act of 2010. The period of performance for the purchase order is anticipated to be a twelve (12) month base period with four (4) option periods of twelve (12) months each. The total estimated value of this purchase order will exceed the simplified acquisition threshold. NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. A request for more information or a copy of the solicitation will not be considered an affirmative response to this Special Notice. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Special Notice will not be accepted. TCSC will consider written responses received no later than 11/30/2026. Responses must be submitted electronically to TCSCAcquisitionOps@.treasury.gov, WRDS /Attn: AM - DV. Responses must include sufficient evidence that clearly shows your company is capable of providing the content described in this notice. Responses received will be evaluated; however, a determination by the Government not to compete the proposed procurement based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no written response is received by the aforementioned deadline that clearly demonstrates an ability to meet all requirements, and that is more advantageous to the Government, TCSC will make award on a sole source basis to the Trustees of the University of Pennsylvania. Qualified Contractors must provide the following: 1. The name and location of your company, contact information, and identify your business size (Large Business, Small Business, Disadvantaged Business, 8(a), Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Business, HUBZone, etc.). Please ensure contact information includes the name of the point of contact, email address, and telephone number, should the Government have questions regarding individual responses. 2. UEI Number. 3. Specific details of the product(s) that your company offers in regards to this notice. 4. Whether your content is available through a Government contract vehicle or Open Market. 5. A brief capabilities statement (not to exceed 5 pages) that includes a description of your company's standard line of business, as well as a list of customers to whom your company currently provides the specific required content. The following file extensions are not allowable and application materials/data submitted with these extensions cannot be considered: .bat, .cmd, .com, .exe, .pif, .rar, .scr, .vbs, .hta, .cpl, and .zip files. Microsoft Office and Adobe compatible documents are acceptable. No other information regarding this Special Notice will be provided at this time. description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. A listing of eligible schedule users can be found at on GSA s website at http://gsa.federalschedules.com/resources/eligible-gsa-schedule-users/. Enter Nationwide if currently/recently providing nationwide (i.e. domestic delivery) coverage. Proposed Coverage: Offerors may propose to provide service to individual states or nationwide. Respond to each question below regarding proposed coverage. For each choice selected, you must also check the box to verify your submission of the requested supporting documentation. description: ***ONLY SEAPORT MAC HOLDERS ARE ELIGIBLE FOR THIS OPPORTUNITY.*** This is a combined Sources Sought/Advance Notice only. The Naval Surface Warfare Center Dahlgren Division (NSWCDD) Gun and Electric Weapon Systems (E Department) has a follow-on requirement for support across multiple effectors, ammunition and weapons systems. See the attached Advance Notice/Sources Sought for additional information. In the event more requests are received than can be accommodated on the afternoon of 19 November 2026, a separate meeting date will be coordinated. Requests for optional one-on-one meetings will not be honored after the registration deadline of 12:00 PM (Noon) EST 18 November 2026. Virtual one-on-one sessions will not be held. Participation in the Industry Day is voluntary and is not required in order to compete for any future solicitation.

description: Request for Information Contract Writing System Recompete 2099AC27N00004 RFI-DO-27-002 The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to identify capable vendors and commercially available solutions that can support the U.S. Department of the Treasury requirements for a contract writing system as part of the Contract Writing System Recompete. SCOPE SUMMARY (See attached Technical Exhibit 1 - Contract Writing System Requirements) The Department of the Treasury is conducting market research to identify qualified vendors capable of providing an enterprise contract writing system solution to support Treasury acquisition and procurement operations. Technical Exhibit 1 identifies anticipated functional, technical, operational, security, hosting, integration, and support requirements designated as Mandatory or Value Added. The Government may use information obtained through this RFI to refine requirements and determine an appropriate acquisition strategy for any future solicitation. The purpose of this Request for Information (RFI) is to gather information from interested vendors regarding their capabilities and potential solutions for a Contract Writing System to support the Department of the Treasury's acquisition and contracting requirements. The incumbent contractor providing the Department's existing Contract Writing System is Unison Software, Inc. II. ANTICIPATED PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for any resulting contract has not been finalized. Interested vendors may be invited to demonstrate their proposed solutions, highlight key features and functionality, and discuss how their offerings could address the Government's operational and technical needs. Participation in any Industry Day or vendor demonstration will be voluntary and at the Government's sole discretion. Additional information regarding scheduling, format, and participation requirements will be provided if the Government determines that such an event would be beneficial. The Government is under no obligation to conduct an Industry Day or vendor demonstrations. Any such activities will be conducted solely for market research and informational purposes and will not constitute a formal evaluation of offers or quotations. Participation or nonparticipation will not guarantee or preclude consideration for, or award of, any future contract. IV. ADDITIONAL DETAILS NO SOLICITATION IS AVAILABLE. Telephone responses or inquiries to this Request for Information will NOT be accepted. description: Revised Language SCOPE OF SOLICITATION The Federal Supply Schedule (FSS) program is also known as the GSA Schedules Program or the Multiple Award Schedule (MAS) Program. The FSS program is directed and managed by GSA and provides Federal agencies with a simplified process for obtaining commercial supplies and services at prices associated with volume buying. Indefinite-delivery, indefinite quantity contracts are awarded to provide supplies and services at stated prices for given periods of time. GSA has delegated authority to the VA to manage the Schedules for medical supplies under the VA FSS program. This solicitation is for the offering of reference laboratory services for the purpose of providing medical laboratory testing for the diagnosis, prevention, or treatment of a disease or condition and to assess patient health to make clinical decisions for patient care.� This solicitation is not for facilities that only collect and/or prepare specimens nor for those facilities that only serve as a mailing service and do not perform testing services. This solicitation is issued to establish contracts which may be used on a nonmandatory basis by eligible users, as a source of supply for the supplies or services described herein, for domestic. Domestic delivery is defined as delivery within the 48 contiguous states, Alaska, Hawaii, Puerto Rico, Washington, DC, and U.S. territories . Offerors may be limited to geographic service areas based upon licensing requirements or may offer nationwide delivery. This solicitation further requires that offered prices cover delivery to destinations (i.e. F.O.B. destination) located within the 48 contiguous states and the District of Columbia. Offerors can choose whether or not prices cover delivery f.o.b. destination to Alaska, Hawaii, and the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico. Additionally, the solicitation defines the number of calendar days after receipt of order (ARO) within which delivery must be made. Offerors who cannot provide the required minimum geographic coverage, that is one state, will not be considered for award. As specified in the solicitation, offerors shall comply with all state, federal and local regulations, licenses, permits, and accreditation necessary to manage and conduct preanalytic specimen testing services. Offerors must comply with states that require out of state licenses/permits. Therefore, laboratories conducting clinical testing on specimens originating in a state that requires an out of state license/permit must hold that state s Department of Health (or other governing body) clinical laboratory permit, licenses, etc. � Offerors that are not compliant with the originating state s licensing and/or permit requirement, regardless of location, will not be considered for an award for that specific state. Offerors may not subcontract to another laboratory to circumvent the originating state s requirement for licensing, permits, etc. The offeror, in itself, is required to meet the requirements of the solicitation without the aid of a subcontractor. The Government retains sole discretion to determine the offeror s capability, compliance, and to limit SINs or geographic coverage. Commercial Items Per GSA regulations at 538.271(a), MAS awards are for commercial items as defined in FAR 2.101. Special Item Numbers (SINs): FSS solicitations set forth broad categories of accepted products/services, referred to as Special Item Numbers (SINs), listed in the Continuation of SF1449 in Vendor Response Document 02. Offerors are not required to submit their entire catalog of products/services but are free to choose which items they will offer as long as those items fall within one of the solicitation s pre-defined SIN categories. Items that do not fall within one of these SINs are considered to be out of scope of the solicitation and cannot be awarded. An item s acceptability under the schedule may be further restricted by a determination of fair and reasonable pricing. Offered diagnostic testing services must be categorized under the accepted services referenced under the Special Item Numbers (SINs) and classified as a specialties or subspecialties of tests as defined under the Clinical Laboratory Improvement Amendments of 1988 (CLIA). Please note that items offered are further restricted to those tests with CPT codes. Additionally, FSS will not award any home diagnostic tests under this schedule. Home diagnostic tests/test kits may be proposed under Schedule 65 V II Invitro Diagnostics, Reagents, Test Kits and Test Sets. FDA Regulatory Requirements Reagents used to perform the tests must be FDA cleared, as appropriate, or be identified as a Laboratory Developed Test (LDT). Offerors of tests not in compliance with these requirements shall not be considered for award under this solicitation. New Items vs. Refurbished or Grey Market Goods This solicitation is for the award of new items only. The Contractor shall provide only new equipment and new parts for the required products described herein. Absolutely no grey market goods or refurbished products shall be provided under any delivery order. Grey market goods are defined as genuine branded goods sold outside of an authorized sales-territory (or by non-authorized dealers in an authorized territory) at prices lower than being charged in authorized sales territories (or by authorized dealers). All equipment must be covered by the manufacturer s warranty. Trade Agreements Act The Trade Agreements Act is applicable to all Schedules. In exercising its authority under FAR Part 25, Foreign Acquisition, purchases by Ordering Activities are restricted to either U.S.-made or designated country end products as defined in clause FAR 52.225-5. For the purposes of this services schedule, origin is determined by the country in which the firm providing the service is established, not the location at which the services are performed. Notice of Additional Requirements - Ordering Level In addition to the terms and conditions set forth in this solicitation, the contractor may, in the performance of orders issued under this contract, be responsible for further requirements at the ordering level. For more information on these potential, additional requirements, please see the note in Solicitation Document 01 after FAR clause 52.216-18 Ordering. Please note that the VA does not promote the use of any company s specific Schedule contract. Vendors should be aware that obtaining a VA Schedule contract is not a guarantee of sales. Vendors awarded a VA Schedule contract will need to market their supplies and services to Government customers as they would to commercial customers. title: Firefox
description: UPDATE: The purpose of Amendment 1 to DARPA-PA-26-137, the Firefox Program Solicitation (PS), is to update the deadlines for OPP submissions and presentations. The Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency (DARPA) has developed a non-invasive coherent optical system capable of recording neural signals in humans. To expand this foundational technology and enable the development of revolutionary, non-invasive brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), DARPA's Firefox program is soliciting approaches to overcome key technological hurdles: 1) development of components enabling dynamic rastering/scanning of the incoming coherent optical signal to target multiple regions of interest and 2) development of new data processing architectures beyond the digital domain to handle the high data rates and computational burden inherent to scaling the amount of neural data recorded by the optical system. The ultimate goal of the Firefox program is to use these innovations to develop a 100-channel, non-invasive BCI with 50-micron spatial and 100-microsecond temporal resolution.

description: The contractor will furnish all labor, transportation, parts, test equipment, tools, and expertise necessary to maintain the Illumina iScan system (Microarray Scanner, Autoloader 2, and 2 Tecan Robots) located at the Central Arkansas VA Medical Center. title: J041--Service - AHU PM & Filter Evaluation - NWI
description: SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE Omaha and Grand Island VAMC - HVAC Preventive Maintenance and Filter Evaluation NAICS: 238220 - PSC: J041 - Small Business Size Standard: $19 million NOTICE PURPOSE The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Network Contracting Office (NCO) 23, is conducting market research to identify businesses capable of providing HVAC preventive maintenance and filter evaluation services at the Omaha and Grand Island VA Medical Centers. This is a sources sought notice only and is not a solicitation or request for quotations. No award will be made from responses, and the Government will not reimburse response costs. GENERAL REQUIREMENT The anticipated requirement includes: Preventive maintenance and inspections of air handling units (AHUs) and rooftop units (RTUs). HVAC equipment and coil cleaning. Air filter inspections and evaluations. Airflow and system performance testing. Humidifier inspection and maintenance. HEPA/MERV filter evaluation and applicable replacement work. Written reports documenting inspections, maintenance, and deficiencies. Services are anticipated for a base year with option years. The detailed requirements will be provided in any resulting solicitation. PLACE OF PERFORMANCE Omaha VA Medical Center, 4101 Woolworth Avenue, Omaha, NE 68105 Grand Island VA Medical Center, 2201 N Broadwell Avenue, Grand Island, NE 68803 INFORMATION REQUESTED Company name, address, UEI, and point of contact with phone number and email. Business size and socioeconomic status, including SBA-certified SDVOSB or VOSB status. Confirmation that the company can perform the services described above at both locations. Brief description of similar HVAC preventive maintenance experience. Whether services would be performed by company employees, subcontractors, or both. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS Email responses no later than Monday, November 30, 2026, at 10:00 a.m. Central Time to amanda.patterson-elliott@va.gov. Use "Omaha and Grand Island HVAC PM Sources Sought" in the subject line. NO PHONE CALL, PLEASE. Responses are for market research purposes only and do not constitute offers.

title: 19WA8026Q0036 - Janitorial services at Embassy office building and Warehouse.
description: Please note this solicitation is not ready to be issued as of this date. The Embassy of the United States in Windhoek will launch the solicitation on the SAM.gov website when it is available. The U.S. Embassy in Windhoek hereby provides the following pre-solicitation notice in respect of the issuance of a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for: Janitorial/cleaning services at the U.S. Embassy Office building and General services warehouse in Windhoek, Namibia. The Contractor shall perform janitorial services in all designated spaces including, but not limited to halls, offices, restrooms, work areas, entrance ways, lobbies, storage areas, elevators, and stairways. The anticipated performance period is for a base year, with four one-year option periods, if exercised by the Government. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, which will be considered. The U.S. Government may award the contract, based on the initial offer, without any discussions. The resultant contract will be a fixed priced type of contract for its duration. The Government is planning a pre-quotation conference and the date for this conference will be in the solicitation. All contractors must be registered in the SAM (System for Award Management) Database https://www.sam.gov prior to submitting an offer pursuant to FAR provision 52.204-7. Therefore, prospective offerors are encouraged to register prior to the submittal of quotations/proposals. This opportunity is subject to 52.229-12 - Tax on Certain Foreign Procurements (FEB 2021) Electronic Submission/Responses: This opportunity allows for electronic responses. Please submit your offer prior to the response date and time. Please ensure your email with your offer does not exceed 15 MB, if it does then you might have to send more than one email. Alternatively, offers may be submitted at the US Embassy offices at the following address: 38 Metje Street, Klein Windhoek, Windhoek, Namibia.

title: NWI Offsite Pathology Services
description: The Department of Veterans Affairs, Nebraska-Western Iowa Health Care System , has a requirement for medical laboratory, pathology and testing analysis services. The Contractor shall be responsible for performing pre-analytic processing as defined in its laboratory manual, analysis, and reporting of analytical results and interpretation for clinical and anatomical pathology specimens as requested by participating facilities (listed below) during the contract period. The contractor shall provide Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services, on a scheduled basis, in accordance with the specifications, terms and conditions herein. VA will be responsible for specimen collection, preparation, grossing (with the exception of, cytology specimens); global surgical pathology cases would require grossing by the contractor. The VA will accession histology and cytology cases, VistA accessioning, preservation and storage of final slides and blocks. All slides and blocks must be returned to the VA for permanent storage. NOTE: The Solicitation number in the announcement 36C26326R0063 was entered incorrectly, however, cannot be changed. The correct solicitation number is 36C26326Q0727. This number has been reconciled throughout the documents.

ALERT: You must submit a notarized letter appointing the authorized Entity Administrator before your registration will be activated. This requirement now applies to both new and existing entities. Effective 29 April 2018, the notarized letter process is now mandatory on all CURRENT registrants at SAM who have a requirement to update data on their SAM record. The notarized letter is mandatory and is required before the GSA Federal Service Desk (FSD) will activate the entity's registration. Effective 29 June 2018, vendors creating or updating their registration can have their registration activated prior to the approval of the required notarized letter. However, the signed copy of the notarized letter must be sent to the GSA Federal Service Desk (FSD) within 30 days of activation or the vendor risks no longer being active in SAM. Remember, there is no cost to use SAM. To find out additional information about the changes of the SAM registration process, contractors should visit the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) link located at the top of the SAM homepage (www.sam.gov).

title: Reagent Generation for Bioanalytical Method Development on Biologics Therapeutics
description: Title: Reagent Generation for Bioanalytical Method Development on Biologics Therapeutics This is a Sources Sought notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The purpose of this notice is to obtain information regarding the availability and capability of all qualified sources to perform a potential requirement. This notice is issued to help determine the availability of qualified companies technically capable of meeting the Government requirement and to determine the method of acquisition. It is not to be construed as a commitment by the Government to issue a solicitation or ultimately award a contract. Responses will not be considered as proposals or quotes. No award will be made as a result of this notice. The Government will NOT be responsible for any costs incurred by the respondents to this notice. This notice is strictly for research and information purposes only. The Government is especially interested in determining (1) the availability of qualified small business sources; (2) whether they are small businesses; HUBZone small businesses; service-disabled, veteran-owned small businesses; 8(a) small businesses; veteran-owned small businesses; woman-owned small businesses; or small disadvantaged businesses; and (3) their size classification relative to the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for the proposed acquisition (5) commercial product and services availability. Your responses to the information requested will assist the Government in determining the appropriate acquisition method, including whether a set-aside is possible. Background: The Therapeutic Development Branch (TDB) within the Division of Preclinical Innovation (DPI) at National Center for Advancing Translational Sciences (NCATS), National Institutes of Health (NIH) conducts translational research in the area of human therapeutics development by moving small molecule and biologic drug candidates forward in the drug development pipeline. Upon reaching predetermined milestones, TDB hands off clinical candidates to external partners to bring these novel therapies to patients. In addition to developing new candidate drugs, TDB seeks to advance the entire field of drug discovery and development by encouraging scientific and technological innovations aimed at improving success rates in the crucial preclinical stage of drug development. The TDB model is to operate as a comprehensive small molecule and biologics drug development organization, moving therapeutic candidates through each phase of the preclinical development process until an Investigational New Drug (IND) application is filed with the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA). TDB conducts drug development as collaborations, with therapeutic candidates originating from academia, industry, non- profit foundations, or internally from NCATS and other NIH Institutes and Centers. TDB�s operational strategy is to combine the capabilities of in-house staff and collaborative partners with complementary support from contract research organizations (CROs). Each development program operates in a multi-disciplinary matrix team environment, with NCATS responsible for the overall planning and execution. Please see the attachment for more details.
