title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - USSF Integration Facility F/10852 at WPAFB
description: SPECIAL NOTICE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a design and construction solicitation for the US Space Force Integration Facility, F/10852 using Progressive Design-Build under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for Construction. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official solicitation release. I. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. II. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 III. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: US Space Force Integration Facility, F/10852 Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH NAICS Code: 236220 Total Program Funding: $394,000,000.00 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The USSF Integration Facility is a newly programmed mission at Wright-Patterson Air Force WPAFB, Ohio. It serves as a highly classified and secured contiguous operations area to enable Director for National Intelligence (DNI) and United States Space Force (USSF) directed and endorsed missions in areas of the highest national security, housing intelligence analysis and production for new and expanded all-source means that enable near-real-time capabilities. The facility supports the intelligence needs of the Defense Intelligence Enterprise, USSF, joint warfighters, policymakers, and acquisition professionals, driving intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance (ISR) for space domain operations including detection, characterization, and targeting of adversary space capabilities. The adjacent existing facility, Building F/10854, will remain fully occupied and uninterrupted, maintaining 24/7 business operations and ICD 705 security accreditation throughout construction, requiring strict utility, access, physical security, and logistical phasing constraints. Construction is broken into distinct agreement phases under the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) framework. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): This Phase is structured to collaboratively advance the facility design from initial concepts to 65% design maturity, perform detailed constructability reviews, conduct transparent open-book cost estimating, identify and mitigate complex interface risks, and validate the overall space programming. Pre-construction services will establish a baseline cost and allow for early design and potential separate authorization of long-lead procurement items. Phase 2 (Final Design and Construction): This Phase will include the completion of final design documents (95% and 100% Certified Final), fast-tracking capabilities, and all physical construction activities, including structural, interior finishes, specialized secure Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) fit-out, redundant systems commissioning, and final security accreditation. Phase 2 will also include comprehensive site work, utility distribution integration, and connection into the active Building F/10854. Phase 2 covers construction of the multi-floor, approximately 333,700 SF secure USSF Integration Facility, including the physical connection to active Building F/10854, the integration of high-efficiency HVAC networks, a backup generator facility, high-security electrical switchgear, and the buildout of specialized SCIF and SAP compartments. The Government will use available concept design information, programmed requirements, and initial planning data as the initial technical baseline. During Phase 1, the selected Design-Builder will validate the baseline and may recommend refinements; any material deviation from the Government�s baseline will require Government review and approval. The scope generally encompasses the following critical lines of effort: Critical Infrastructure and Utilities: Installation of high-efficiency mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems designed for 24/7 continuous operation, electrical tie-ins to centralized utilities, backup generator integration (7,500 KW), Lightning Protection Systems (LPS), and addressable fire protection networks. Secure Facilities: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of highly classified Special Access Program (SAP) SCIF spaces built to stringent ICD 705, IC Tech Spec, and Telecommunictaions Electronics Material Protected from Emanating Spurious Tranmission (TEMPEST) shielding standards to ensure complete physical, visual, and acoustic isolation. New Construction, Envelope, and Physical Connection: Construction of a new structural frame with metal panels and pre-cast exterior walls, establishing a secure thermal wall envelope, executing the physical and utility connection to adjacent operational Building F/10854, and conducting all associated site work, paving, and access control infrastructure. V. ACQUISITION STRATEGY - PRE-AWARD The USACE will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 �RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitches: Selected Companies will participate in pitch presentations. One company will be selected as the Design-Build team for award of the initial design and preconstruction services with a modification for design completion and construction award. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. VI. ACQUSITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified Progressive Design-Build Entity (PDBE) to provide design development, preconstruction services, and construction. description: Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Page 2 of 2 Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution INTRODUCTION This is a Request for Information (RFI) notice for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products described in this notice. Your response to this RFI notice will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI notice. This RFI notice does not constitute a solicitation for quotes/proposals or the authority to enter negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI notice. Not responding to this RFI notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation should one be issued. Any Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) or Veteran-owned small businesses (VOSBs) responding to this RFI notice must include their intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort in accordance with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-73 or 852.219-74, VA Notice of Total Set-Aside for SDVOSB or VOSB respectively. Specifically, the requirement for at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing or 50% of the services be performed by yourself and/or other eligible and Small Business Administration verified SDVOSB/VOSB concerns; and certification from the Small Business Administration (VetCert). It is requested that all companies interested in participating in this RFI please note their interest and provide indication of their respective capabilities to perform the potential effort, as described in the paragraphs below and the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) Description. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI notice is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. VA reserves the right to not respond to any, all, or select responses or materials submitted. All requirements identified herein are subject to change at any time. The purpose of this RFI notice is for planning purposes, to identify market information and qualified contractors who are able to meet VA s requirement for Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution. Any information provided in response to this RFI notice may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement, as well as determining any set-aside decisions. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with a size standard of 34 Million. Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI notice. Responses shall be as complete and informative as possible. It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor this site for updates and/or additional information pertaining to this requirement. BACKGROUND: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology, Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC), requires an enterprise database vulnerability scanning solution to support recurring security assessments and Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. VA currently uses LevelBlue Trustwave DbProtect across four production environments and one development environment. The existing capability includes centralized management, distributed scanning, vulnerability assessment content, reporting and analytics, and supporting repository and data-processing functions. Scanning components operate on premises and within VA Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure environments. Management, reporting, and repository functions are hosted on premises. The current repository retains 12 months of scan information and uses approximately 3.17 terabytes (TB) of storage. VA conducts monthly enterprise scanning and daily on-demand scans supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. The current solution assesses at least 1,700 multi-vendor enterprise database targets within a 3-week period each month without adversely affecting the performance or availability of active ATO scanning. Database owners establish authorized scan windows and operational restrictions. The database inventory in the Draft PWS reflects VA s current environment and may change during the contract period. VA may add database types supported by the proposed solution, including those supported through standard product updates, during the base period or any exercised option period. Support for these additional database types shall be included at no additional cost to the Government, provided the total number of database assets remains within the enterprise licensed capacity required by the Draft PWS. The Contractor shall identify any database-specific licensing restrictions or additional charges in its proposal. If interested and capable of providing for this requirement, please see the Response Instructions and Submission Instruction sections below. title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - USSF Integration Facility F/10852 at WPAFB
description: SPECIAL NOTICE The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a design and construction solicitation for the US Space Force (USSF) Integration Facility, F/10852 using Progressive Design-Build under 10 USC �2808a Other Transaction Authority for Construction. This notice is for informational and planning purposes to allow interested parties to prepare for and provide feedback prior to the official solicitation release. I. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input in advance of the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. II. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 III. PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: US Space Force (USSF) Integration Facility, F/10852 Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH NAICS Code: 236220 Total Program Funding: $394,000,000.00 IV. PROJECT DESCRIPTION The USSF Integration Facility is a newly programmed mission at Wright-Patterson Air Force WPAFB, Ohio. This classified and contiguous operations area ultimately supports USSF�s mission to secure our Nation�s interest in, from, and to space as well as support across the Defense the Intelligence Enterprise. The new facility is situated adjacent to Building F/10854 to enable collaboration with partners and thus requires strict coordination for future utility access, physical security and logistics. Construction is broken into distinct agreement phases under the Progressive Design-Build (PDB) framework. Phase 1 (Design & Pre-Construction): This Phase is structured to collaboratively advance the facility design from initial concepts to 65% design maturity, perform detailed constructability reviews, conduct transparent open-book cost estimating, identify and mitigate complex interface risks, and validate the overall space programming. Pre-construction services will establish a baseline cost and allow for early design and potential separate authorization of long-lead procurement items. Phase 2 (Final Design and Construction): This Phase will include the completion of final design documents (95% and 100% Certified Final), fast-tracking capabilities, and all physical construction activities, including structural, interior finishes, specialized secure controlled space, redundant systems commissioning, and final security accreditation. Phase 2 will also include comprehensive site work, utility distribution integration, and connection into the active Building F/10854. Phase 2 covers construction of the multi-floor, approximately 333,700 SF secure USSF Integration Facility, including the physical connection to active Building F/10854, the integration of high-efficiency HVAC networks, a backup generator facility, high-security electrical switchgear, and the buildout of specialized controlled space. The Government will use available concept design information, programmed requirements, and initial planning data as the initial technical baseline. During Phase 1, the selected Design-Builder will validate the baseline and may recommend refinements; any material deviation from the Government�s baseline will require Government review and approval. The scope generally encompasses the following critical lines of effort: Critical Infrastructure and Utilities: Installation of high-efficiency mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC) systems designed for 24/7 continuous operation, electrical tie-ins to centralized utilities, replacement of two existing end-of-life generators with new, Lightning Protection Systems (LPS), and addressable fire protection networks. Secure Facilities: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of highly classified controlled space built to stringent ICD 705, IC Tech Spec, and Telecommunictaions Electronics Material Protected from Emanating Spurious Tranmission (TEMPEST) shielding standards to ensure complete physical, visual, and acoustic isolation. New Construction, Envelope, and Physical Connection: Construction of a new structural frame with metal panels and pre-cast exterior walls, establishing a secure thermal wall envelope, executing the physical and utility connection to adjacent operational Building F/10854, and conducting all associated site work, paving, and access control infrastructure. V. ACQUISITION STRATEGY - PRE-AWARD The USACE will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 �RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitches: Selected Companies will participate in pitch presentations. One company will be selected as the Design-Build team for award of the initial design and preconstruction services with a modification for design completion and construction award. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. VI. ACQUSITION STRATEGY � AWARD The agreement will be awarded to the most qualified progressive design-build entity (PDBE) to provide design development, preconstruction services, and construction. Post-award Phase 1 of PDB includes Design and Pre-construction services and Post-award Phase 2 includes the final design and construction. The agreement will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). The FFP for successive design and construction milestones will be agreed to as the design progresses and funds are available. VII. VIRTUAL PARTICIPATION OPPORTUNITY: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r VIII. KEY SECURITY REQUIREMENTS This project will require the selected contractor and its subcontractor(s) to process, store, or transmit CUI and Federal Contract Information (FCI). In accordance with the CMMC program (32 CFR part 170) and USACE policy (including Alert 26-HQ-010, Rev1), CMMC Level 2 (Self) will be a mandatory prerequisite prior to award. Offerors must have an active SAM registration and a current, verified BASIC confidence level assessment (or higher) posted in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) in accordance with NIST SP 800-171. NOTE: An offeror will not be eligible for award if they do not possess the required CMMC status posted in SPRS prior to award. IX. CLOSING STATEMENT All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal solicitation.

The Contractor shall be responsible for performing pre-analytic processing as defined in its laboratory manual, analysis, and reporting of analytical results and interpretation for clinical and anatomical pathology specimens as requested by participating facilities (listed below) during the contract period. The contractor shall provide Pathology and Laboratory Medicine Services, on a scheduled basis, in accordance with the specifications, terms and conditions herein. VA will be responsible for specimen collection, preparation, grossing (with the exception of, cytology specimens); global surgical pathology cases would require grossing by the contractor. The VA will accession histology and cytology cases, VistA accessioning, preservation and storage of final slides and blocks. All slides and blocks must be returned to the VA for permanent storage. NOTE: The Solicitation number in the announcement 36C26326R0063 was entered incorrectly, however, cannot be changed. The correct solicitation number is 36C26326Q0727. This number has been reconciled throughout the documents.

title: Mid-Bay James Island Restoration Phase 2
description: This Invitation for Bid (IFB) solicitation is for the restoration work at James Island, Dorchester County, Maryland. James Island is an ecosystem restoration project (part of the Mid-Chesapeake Bay Island Ecosystem Restoration project, commonly referred to as Mid-Bay) located in the middle Chesapeake Bay in Dorchester County, Maryland, approximately 56 miles south-southeast of the Port of Baltimore and one mile north of Taylors Island.

title: DA10--Office of Information & Technology Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution
description: Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Page 2 of 2 Request for Information 36C10B27Q0010 Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution INTRODUCTION This is a Request for Information (RFI) notice for planning purposes only and shall not be considered an Invitation for Bid, Request for Task Execution Plan, Request for Quotation, or a Request for Proposal. Additionally, there is no obligation on the part of the Government to acquire any products described in this notice. Your response to this RFI notice will be treated only as information for the Government to consider. You will not be entitled to payment for direct or indirect costs that you incur in responding to this RFI notice. This RFI notice does not constitute a solicitation for quotes/proposals or the authority to enter negotiations to award a contract. No funds have been authorized, appropriated, or received for this effort. Interested parties are responsible for adequately marking proprietary, restricted, or competition sensitive information contained in their response. The Government does not intend to pay for the information submitted in response to this RFI notice. Not responding to this RFI notice does not preclude participation in any future solicitation should one be issued. Any Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs) or Veteran-owned small businesses (VOSBs) responding to this RFI notice must include their intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort in accordance with the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 852.219-73 or 852.219-74, VA Notice of Total Set-Aside for SDVOSB or VOSB respectively. Specifically, the requirement for at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing or 50% of the services be performed by yourself and/or other eligible and Small Business Administration verified SDVOSB/VOSB concerns; and certification from the Small Business Administration (VetCert). It is requested that all companies interested in participating in this RFI please note their interest and provide indication of their respective capabilities to perform the potential effort, as described in the paragraphs below and the Draft Performance Work Statement (PWS) Description. Any information submitted by respondents to this RFI notice is strictly voluntary. All submissions become Government property and will not be returned. VA reserves the right to not respond to any, all, or select responses or materials submitted. All requirements identified herein are subject to change at any time. The purpose of this RFI notice is for planning purposes, to identify market information and qualified contractors who are able to meet VA s requirement for Enterprise Database Vulnerability Scanning Solution. Any information provided in response to this RFI notice may be used by VA in developing its acquisition strategy and Performance Work Statement, as well as determining any set-aside decisions. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) for this requirement is 541519, Other Computer Related Services, with a size standard of 34 Million. Be advised that set-aside decisions may be made based on the information provided in response to this RFI notice. Responses shall be as complete and informative as possible. It is the responsibility of interested parties to monitor this site for updates and/or additional information pertaining to this requirement. BACKGROUND: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), Office of Information and Technology, Cybersecurity Operations Center (CSOC), requires an enterprise database vulnerability scanning solution to support recurring security assessments and Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. VA currently uses LevelBlue Trustwave DbProtect across four production environments and one development environment. The existing capability includes centralized management, distributed scanning, vulnerability assessment content, reporting and analytics, and supporting repository and data-processing functions. Scanning components operate on premises and within VA Amazon Web Services (AWS) and Microsoft Azure environments. Management, reporting, and repository functions are hosted on premises. The current repository retains 12 months of scan information and uses approximately 3.17 terabytes (TB) of storage. VA conducts monthly enterprise scanning and daily on-demand scans supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities. The current solution assesses at least 1,700 multi-vendor enterprise database targets within a 3-week period each month without adversely affecting the performance or availability of active ATO scanning. Database owners establish authorized scan windows and operational restrictions. The database inventory in the Draft PWS reflects VA s current environment and may change during the contract period. VA may add database types supported by the proposed solution, including those supported through standard product updates, during the base period or any exercised option period. Support for these additional database types shall be included at no additional cost to the Government, provided the total number of database assets remains within the enterprise licensed capacity required by the Draft PWS. The Contractor shall identify any database-specific licensing restrictions or additional charges in its proposal. If interested and capable of providing for this requirement, please see the Response Instructions and Submission Instruction sections below. RESPONSE INSTRUCTIONS: All responsible sources may submit a response in accordance with the information below: NO MARKETING MATERIALS ARE ALLOWED AS PART OF THIS RFI NOTICE. Be advised that generic capability statements will not be reviewed. Responses should be as complete and informative as possible. Interested Vendors shall submit the following: The initial paragraph of the submission shall include the following information and responses to the RFI Questions: Name of Company: Address: Point of Contact: Phone Number: Email Address: Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): NAICS code(s)*: 541519 Company Business Size & Status for above NAICS: Socioeconomic Data: If a small business, please identify socio-economic category(ies). Indicate the likelihood of your company responding to a solicitation should this effort result in an acquisition. Note: Small businesses should include intent and ability to meet set-aside requirements for performance of this effort, if applicable. Existing Contractual Vehicles (GWAC, FSS or MAC): If recommending a solution other than VA s current LevelBlue DbProtect solution, provide major milestones and timelines from building the new architecture to meeting the Government s requirement of monthly enterprise scanning and daily on-demand scans supporting Authorization to Operate (ATO) activities, including at least 1,700 multi-vendor enterprise database targets within a 3-week period each month without adversely affecting the performance or availability of active ATO scanning Provide, in detail, what VA infrastructure, network access, and staff support would be required for implementation. title: Progressive Design-Build (PDB) - RENOVATE HQ AFMC B/10262 PH 2 at WPAFB
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) is issuing this special notice to announce an upcoming competition for a construction solicitation for the Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC) Headquarters (HQ) Renovation, Building 10262, utilizing an Other Transaction (OT) Agreement under 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The anticipated delivery method is Progressive Design-Build (PDB). This notice is for informational and planning purposes. INDUSTRY DAY USACE intends to conduct an Industry Day on 03 December 2026 at 0900 Eastern Time to provide an overview of the project, acquisition strategy, and anticipated requirements. This event will provide interested parties with an opportunity to gain additional insight into the project and proposed PDB under an OT (non-FAR-based) framework. A notional acquisition schedule will be shared. Interested parties are encouraged to ask questions and provide input in advance of the official Request for Qualifications (RFQ) release. General questions will be permitted during the Industry Day; however, all discussions and responses provided during the event are considered unofficial and are for informational purposes only. Statements made during the Industry Day do not constitute commitment, authorization, or binding guidance related to the future RFQ. Official Questions and Answers (Q&A) will be accepted and addressed following the release of RFQ. LOCATION Industry Day Presentation location: Hope Hotel, 10823 Chidlaw Rd # A, Dayton, OH 45433 PROJECT OVERVIEW Project Title: Renovate Headquarters (HQ) Air Force Materiel Command (AFMC), Building 10262, Phase 2 Construction Location: Wright-Patterson Air Force Base (WPAFB), OH Agency: U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Louisville District NAICS Code: 236220 PROJECT DESCRIPTION This acquisition will deliver the design and construction for the progressive design-build phased renovation of Building 10262, AFMC HQ, at WPAFB, OH. The scope of work consists of furnishing all necessary equipment, materials, labor, supervision, quality control, and supplies to deliver a fully functional, modernized headquarters facility while supporting ongoing occupied command operations. Key features of the project may include: Facility Renewal, Envelope, and Interior Renovation: Replacement of the Building 10262 roof and related envelope work, comprehensive interior renovation and finishes of the entire second floor, designated basement areas, required building repairs, and hazardous-material abatement. Critical Infrastructure Overhaul: Modernization and replacement of affected mechanical, electrical, plumbing (MEP), heating, ventilation, and air conditioning (HVAC), electric-power, telecommunications, fire-protection, fire-alarm, and life-safety systems necessary to support the renovated areas. Secure Facilities & Specialized Spaces: Turnkey design, construction, and Defense Intelligence Agency (DIA) accreditation of Special Access Program (SAP) and Sensitive Compartmented Information Facility (SCIF) spaces compliant with ICD 705 / IC Tech Spec and DoDM 5205.07 Vol 3 standards (including designated basement areas). Occupied Facility Logistics & Continuity: Construction sequencing, utility/system outage planning, temporary bypass systems, controlled access, and strict coordination to maintain uninterrupted global command operations supporting approximately 4,000 personnel. ACQUISITION STRATEGY � PRE-AWARD USACE � Louisville District will use a streamlined competitive selection process: Step 1 � RFQ: Interested parties will submit a Statement of Qualifications (SOQ). Following evaluation of the qualification packages, the Government intends to short-list a target of three (3) of the highest qualified Design-Builders to proceed to Step 2. Step 2 � Pitch Presentations: Short-listed firms must attend a mandatory site visit at WPAFB, OH during pitch preparation, followed by live, interactive presentations. Problem-solving, technical approach, risk management, and team chemistry will be evaluated by the Government. Step 3 � Exclusive Negotiation: Based on pitch evaluations, the Government will select one Design-Builder to enter exclusive negotiations. All interested parties should monitor the official solicitation announcement, which will provide complete details and submission instructions. Draft documents may be provided at a future date for feedback and informational purposes only and are subject to change upon issuance of the formal project RFQ. Virtual Participation Opportunity: For those who are unable to attend the Industry Day event in person, the Louisville District will also make the event available via Microsoft Teams. The details related to the MS Teams event are provided below: Microsoft Teams Meeting Join: https://dod.teams.microsoft.us/meet/993610255621?p=yaQ28DL3lmCC9Nap5C Meeting ID: 993 610 255 621 Passcode: Y6sB764r This is a combined Industry Day for AFMC and United States Space Force (USSF).

title: France – Technical assistance services – Prestations d'assistance technique "mission d'animateur sécurité et environnement", pour le compte du CEA, centre de Valduc
description: Les prestations comprennent plusieurs activités d'assistance à l'exploitation et à la sécurité de certaines installations du CEA Centre de Valduc (avec une partie des bâtiments à caractère industriel et nucléaire) telles que : - des diagnostics et analyses de sécurité (compléter des autorisations d'intervention, des convocations et plans de prévention, rédaction de rapports de contrôle, de déroulement d'opération, d'accident de travail, etc), - des analyses/évaluations des risques (création de mode opératoire, rédaction de bilan de sécurité, mise à jour de dossiers d'évaluation des risques, etc), - des actions de prévention (création et mise à jour de consigne de sécurité, mise à jour de fiches d'unité de travail, planification des accueils sécurité, création de divers supports de présentation, mise à jour des divers plans de sécurité, rédaction de comptes-rendus, etc), - de la gestion des produits chimiques (inventaire et mise à jour des classeurs de fiches de données de sécurité).

title: Saltash Guildhall Internal Works
description: Saltash Town Council is seeking tenders from suitably qualified contractors for internal remodelling works at the Guildhall, Lower Fore Street, Saltash. The project comprises refurbishment and adaptation works to support revised council operations and meeting functions, including: Manufacture and installation of bespoke horseshoe-shaped council chamber desking accommodating approximately 20 members/users. Supply and installation of audio visual equipment to support hybrid meetings, Microsoft Teams connectivity, microphones, displays, speakers and associated control systems. Installation of an assisted listening system. Electrical alterations and new power and data infrastructure within the First Floor Long Room. Electrical and data alterations within the Ground Floor Council Chamber. Electrical and data alterations within the Clerk's Office. Heating alterations including replacement radiators within the Council Chamber. Supply and installation of acoustic underlay and new carpet finishes within the First Floor Long Room. Associated commissioning, testing, certification, training and making good. The works will be undertaken within an occupied civic building and contractors must maintain safe operation of the premises throughout the contract period.

description: Presolicitation Notice Presolicitation Notice Page 3 of 3 Presolicitation Notice *=Required Field Presolicitation Notice Page 1 of 3 THIS OPPORTUNITY IS AVAILABLE ONLY TO SERVICE-DISABLED VETERAN-OWNED SMALL BUSINESSES. The Pineville LA VA Medical Center has a requirement for a chiller replacement. The contractor shall provide all labor, materials, tools, equipment, expertise, administration, supervision transportation and anything else necessary to perform all work as described in project Scope of Work, Drawings, and Specifications. This acquisition will be solicited pursuant to the Veterans' First Public Law 109-461 as a 100% Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Set-Aside (SDVOSB). At least 15 percent of the cost of the contract performance incurred for personnel shall be spent on the concern's employees or the employees of other eligible SDVOSB concerns. Please do not send questions to this notice as it is only a Pre-Solicitation Notice. Questions will be accepted only after the solicitation has been published. Check SAM for the Solicitation. Solicitation documents, including specifications and drawings, will be available electronically on or about October 27, 2026, on this website. Hard copies will not be mailed. INTERESTED PARTIES ARE STRONGLY ENCOURAGED TO REGISTER TO RECEIVE NOTIFICATION OF ACTIONS INCLUDING POSTING OF THE SOLICITATION AND ANY AMENDMENTS. ADDITIONALLY, OFFERORS ARE ADVISED TO CHECK THE SITE FREQUENTLY AS THEY ARE RESPONSIBLE FOR OBTAINING AMENDMENTS TO THE SOLICITATION NOTICE. A 90-day proposal acceptance period will be required. A bid bond must be submitted with the proposal. Performance and Payment bonds will be required from the contractor receiving the award. The magnitude of construction is between $100,000.00 and $250,000.00. North American Industrial Classification Standard (NAICS) code assigned to this construction project is 238220 with a small business size standard of $19 million in average annual receipts for the past three (3) years. Offerors shall be registered with SBA VetCert at Veteran Small Business Certification (sba.gov), in System for Award Management (SAM) database at www.sam.gov and have completed online Representations and Certifications prior to the solicitation due date. Offerors shall be registered with the NAICS code assigned to this acquisition in VetCert.

description: This Notice of Intent is not a request for competitive proposals. This is not a solicitation or request for offers. title: Notice of Intent to Award a Sole Source KeyTrak Maintenance
description: This is a NOTICE OF INTENT TO AWARD A SOLE SOURCE CONTRACT in accordance with: � FAR 6.103-1 and Title 10 United States Code (U.S.C.) � 3204(a)(1) ("Only one responsible source and no other supplies or services will satisfy agency requirements"); � FAR Subpart 12.2 / FAR 12.201-1 ("Simplified Procedures for Commercial Products and Commercial Services"); and The Mission and Installation Contracting Command (MICC) Fort Benning, on behalf of the Directorate of Training Sustainment (DOTS), intends to negotiate and award a sole-source, Firm-Fixed-Price purchase order/contract to: � Contractor: KEY-TECH SALES & SERVICES, LLC The Directorate of Training Sustainment (DOTS) has an immediate and continuous operational requirement for specialized preventative maintenance, corrective diagnostic repair, micro-controller calibration, and hardware upkeep for its existing inventory of four (4) KeyTrak electronic key storage systems deployed across Fort Benning. The scope of work encompasses: � Third-Party Technical Maintenance & Emergency Repair: Performance of scheduled operational maintenance, routine calibrations, and on-call corrective repairs to maintain full mechanical and electronic operability of the four KeyTrak key storage enclosures. � Component Replacement & Hardware Support: Sourcing and installation of compatible replacement components, including locking solenoids, power distribution modules, micro-controller boards, and key-tag tracking interfaces to prevent system failure. � Preservation of Chain-of-Custody & Physical Security Safeguards: Ensuring continuous, zero-downtime key-control management to maintain audit tracking and physical security protocols for government fleet vehicles, arms/ammunition supply areas, and secured facilities across the installation. Based on technical market analysis, KEY-TECH SALES & SERVICES, LLC is currently the sole identified commercial provider possessing the requisite diagnostic tooling, technician proficiency, and supply chain access for KeyTrak-compatible replacement components necessary to maintain these four installed units without mission failure. This notice of intent is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed action based upon responses received is solely within the discretion of the Government. Information received will normally be considered solely for the purpose of determining whether to conduct a competitive procurement in the future. Any alternative contractor proposing to satisfy this requirement must demonstrate independent technical capability, technician experience, and verified access to KeyTrak-compatible replacement parts and diagnostic equipment without causing unacceptable operational downtime. Replacing the existing installed KeyTrak infrastructure with an entirely new key control platform would cause the Government substantial duplication of unrecoverable costs (including hardware procurement, facility mounting, network reconfiguration, and disposal) alongside severe disruption to mission operations. Interested organizations that believe they possess the technical capability and component supply access to satisfy this requirement without unacceptable delay or substantial duplication of cost may submit a technical capability statement. Responses must include the following information: 1. Company Name and Physical Address. 2. Technical Capability Statement demonstrating independent technical expertise, diagnostic methodology, and past performance maintaining and repairing KeyTrak electronic key storage systems. 3. Supply Chain Verification detailing access to reliable replacement hardware and components (e.g., locking solenoids, micro-controllers, circuit boards, and key tags) compatible with KeyTrak units. 4. SAM CAGE Code and Unique Entity ID (UEI). 5. Point of Contact Information (Name, title, telephone number, and official corporate email address). 6. Business Size Status in relation to NAICS code 561621 / PSC J063. All inquiries and capability responses must be submitted via email. No telephone inquiries or verbal requests will be accepted. Notice of Intent Contacts: � Contract Specialist: Aaliyah Giadoo Email: Aaliyah.c.giadoo.civ@army.mil � Contracting Officer: Stacia Rivers Email: Stacia.m.rivers.civ@army.mil

title: R799--Lake Baldwin EUL Development Opportunity Sources Sought COR: Dustin Koonce
description: Lake Baldwin VA Clinic, FL EUL Request for Expressions of Interest 1 REQUEST FOR EXPRESSIONS OF INTEREST ENHANCED-USE LEASE DEVELOPMENT OPPORTUNITY Orlando Healthcare System Veterans Integrated Service Network 08 (VISN 08) Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic - Orlando, FL Notice This advertisement is a notice of a potential opportunity. This Request for Expressions of Interest (the advertisement ) is not a solicitation for offers, nor is it a request for proposals. Respondents are advised that the Government assumes no responsibility to award an Enhanced-Use Lease (EUL) based upon responses to this advertisement. This Sources Sought Notice is to identify potential sources for information and planning purposes only and is not intended to pre-qualify or disqualify any potential Respondents. The purpose of this Sources Sought is to conduct market research to determine if there are responsible and qualified entities interested in redeveloping the assets described in Section III and if yes, what potential reuse options exist. The information gained from this Sources Sought will be used to assist the Government in determining if this development opportunity can be competitive and/or a total Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB) or Veteran-Owned Small Business (VOSB) Set-Aside. The Government will use this information to determine the best acquisition strategy for this procurement and to inform related asset management decision-making. The Government requests that interested parties respond to this Notice with the specific information requested in Section V of this Notice and identify their small business status. VA is particularly interested in SDVOSB/VOSB respondents capabilities to perform a minimum of 51% of the development opportunity described in this Notice. Developers responding to this market research should be aware that responding to this advertisement may not ensure that they qualify for any underlying future solicitation or contract award. Responding to this Sources Sought Notice is NOT a prerequisite to respond to any future subsequent solicitations. The Government will not reimburse participants for any expenses associated with their participation in this Sources Sought. The Government cannot provide any warranty, expressed or implied, as to the accuracy, reliability or completeness of the information contained in this Notice. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. An EUL is a long-term ground lease of underutilized VA-owned land or buildings to a non-federal entity (Developer). Under the EUL program, the Developer secures a long-term leasehold interest with VA for the subject property. This deal structure enables developers to finance, design, develop, renovate/construct, operate, and maintain improvements on VA property to directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. The objective of this development opportunity is to repurpose assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic under VA s EUL Program to the benefit of Veterans. Respondents should consider the following as they formulate responses to this Notice: Lease-back by VA or other Federal government entities is not permissible, and financing cannot reflect a lease-back arrangement. The PACT Act does not nullify 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(5), which states, "The terms of an enhanced-use lease may not provide for any acquisition, contract, demonstration, exchange, grant, incentive, procurement, sale, other transaction authority, service agreement, use agreement, lease, or lease-back by the Secretary or Federal Government. VA may only receive cash consideration for ground lease rent in an EUL (per 38 U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(B)). This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). Additional information on the VA s EUL program and sample EUL projects may be obtained at: http://www.va.gov/assetmanagement/. Development Scope The intent of this Notice is to determine if there are experienced developers, including SDVOSB or VOSB developers, that can develop the subject assets in accordance with VA s EUL authority. The Developer would undertake all necessary investigative activities to develop the selected assets at the Lake Baldwin VA Medical Clinic campus. VA is especially interested in development of supportive housing but will also consider other uses that benefit Veterans. Overview and Objectives The United States Department of Veterans Affairs (VA), under its Enhanced-Use Leasing (EUL) authority (38 U.S.C. §§ 8161- 8169, as amended), is seeking expressions of interest from qualified developers, including SDVOSBs and VOSBs, to serve as a Developer for purposes of developing supportive housing or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans (e.g., general affordable housing, skilled nursing facilities, technical job training centers, research facilities, mixed-use, other). VA s EUL authority allows VA to outlease land and improvements to selected developers (i.e., Lessees) to provide housing and/or other uses that directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. Such leases can have a term of up to 99 years. VA s Office of Asset Enterprise Management (OAEM) administers the EUL Program. An EUL is a long-term ground lease of underutilized VA-owned land or buildings to a non-federal entity (Developer). Under the EUL program, the Developer secures a long-term leasehold interest with VA for the subject property. This deal structure enables developers to finance, design, develop, renovate/construct, operate, and maintain improvements on VA property to directly or indirectly benefit Veterans. This means VA cannot receive any in-kind consideration or free/discounted services as part of a new EUL agreement. However, projects may provide free or discounted services to individual Veterans or Veteran Service Organizations, and the Secretary may enter into an EUL without receiving consideration per U.S.C. § 8162(b)(3)(C). title: 6810--501 - Dry Ice Base +4
description: The purpose of this amendment is to answer questions regarding Pre-solicitation Notice 36C26227Q0115. Q: Is 5/8 inch a strict nominal diameter, or is there an allowable tolerance? Would nominal 1/2-inch pellets be acceptable? A: 5/8 inch is preferred but 1/2 inch would be acceptable. No larger than 3/4 inch. Q: What documentation should offerors provide to demonstrate that the proposed container meets the stated specifications and the target of less than 8% sublimation loss per 24 hours? A: Manufacture documentation will be required. Q: The notice lists both 7:30 a.m. 3:00 p.m. and 8:00 a.m. 3:30 p.m. Mountain Time. Which window applies to the receiving dock at 2401 Centre Ave SE? A: 7:30 am 3:00 pm MT Q: Would the VA accept two insulated containers containing 300 lbs each, for a combined weekly delivery of 600 lbs, instead of a single container with a minimum capacity of 700 lbs? A: The weekly delivery must be at least 550lbs and no more than 600lbs in a single container. Q: Would the VA accept weekly deliveries on Thursdays or Fridays instead of Mondays, provided we consistently deliver the required 600 lbs? Thursday would be our preferred delivery day, subject to confirmation of our ability to maintain that schedule. A: Thursday/Friday delivery will lead to excess waste and will not be appropriate for the hospital s scheduled send-outs. Q: Could you confirm whether November 26, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Pacific is the deadline for responding to the pre-solicitation or for submitting a formal quote? Please also let us know where the solicitation and submission instructions will be available. A: The date and time, extended to Monday, November 30, 2026, at 9:00 a.m. Pacific Time, is the deadline for responding to the pre-solicitation notice and expressing interest in the requirement. It is not the deadline for submission of a formal quote. The Government intends to issue the solicitation directly to vendors determined capable of meeting the requirement based on: Vendors identified through market research. Vendors known to carry the required product. Vendors capable of meeting delivery requirements. Vendors that satisfy the socioeconomic requirement. Past performance. Price. Q: Should each annual CLIN be quoted as a single delivered price per pound that includes delivery, fuel, hazmat fees, and container exchange? A: Yes. Q: Will a supplier's weight ticket be sufficient to verify the 600-pound net delivery, or does the receiving team weigh it on site? A: Weight tickets will be sufficient. Q: Should the driver exchange containers at the dock or move them to a designated storage area? How should the driver handle any dry ice remaining in the previous container? A: Any remaining dry ice from previous deliveries will be transferred before exchanges, which will occur at the dock. Receiving personnel will move the deliveries to the storage area. Q: Does SBA's class waiver of the nonmanufacturer rule for industrial gases (NAICS 325120, PSC 6810) apply to this requirement, or must the dry ice be produced by a small business manufacturer? A: The nonmanufacturer rule will apply to this requirement. Q: May the contractor's supplier own the insulated storage containers and swap them at each weekly delivery? A: Yes. Q: Can invoicing occur weekly? A: Invoices will need to be submitted monthly, in arrears.

description: This is a notice of intent, not a request for a quotation. A solicitation document will not be issued and quotations will not be requested. This procurement is acquisition is to continue to obtain Soft software and hardware license and maintenance services for the IBM hardware and AIX operating system for servers that support the existing Laboratory Information System (LIS). Soft Computer Corporation (SCC) has been the incumbent since the initial install of the software and due to its proprietary nature they have performed the ongoing maintenance and support on the system. The current LIS software system is proprietary to SCC who developed it. SCC does not permit 3rd party maintenance and will not release their source code to other entities. As the LIS modules in the Clinical Center are currently handling large volumes of patient data and test and diagnostic results, it is absolutely imperative that there be no interruption in the ongoing operation/functioning of the existing system. Patient safety is of great concern if there is a system failure or interruption in service. Therefore it is critical that the system continues to be maintained by SCC who is the only source capable of providing the necessary maintenance, including making revisions to the source code as circumstances may dictate. Because the LIS helps support patient diagnosis and care activities, it is deemed a mission critical system for the Clinical Center. The proprietary status of the system to SCC clearly demonstrates that they are the only firm qualified to perform the required maintenance services. This acquisition is being conducted using policies unique to the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 13 �Simplified Acquisition Procedures, Subpart 13.500 This subpart authorizes the use of simplified procedures for the acquisition of supplies and services in amounts greater than the simplified acquisition threshold but not exceeding $9 million ($15 million for acquisitions as described in 13.500(c)), including options, if the contracting officer reasonably expects, based on the nature of the supplies or services sought, and on market research, that offers will include only commercial products or commercial services. Contracting officers may use any simplified acquisition procedure in this part, subject to any specific dollar limitation applicable to the particular procedure. Contracts awarded using FAR Part 13-Simplified Acquisition Procedures are exempt from the requirements of FAR Part 6-Competition Requirements. DISCLAIMER: THIS SOURCES SOUGHT IS FOR INFORMATIONAL PURPOSES ONLY. THIS IS NOT A REQUEST FOR PROPOSAL (RFP), REQUEST FOR QUOTE (RFQ) OR AN INVITATION FOR BID (IFB). IN ACCORDANCE WITH FAR 15.201(e), THIS NOTICE DOES NOT CONSTITUTE A SOLICITATION AND SHALL NOT BE CONSTRUED AS A COMMITMENT BY THE GOVERNMENT. RESPONSES IN ANY FORM ARE NOT OFFERS AND THE GOVERNMENT IS UNDER NO OBLIGATION TO AWARD A CONTRACT AS A RESULT OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT.NO FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE TO PAY FOR PREPARATION OF RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT. ANY INFORMATION SUBMITTED BY RESPONDENTS TO THIS TECHNICAL DESCRIPTION IS STRICTLY VOLUNTARY. THE GOVERNMENT MAY USE THE INFORMATION OBTAINED FROM RESPONSES TO THIS NOTICE IN DETERMINING ITS ACQUISITION APPROACH. THE ISSUANCE OF THIS NOTICE DOES NOT RESTRICT THE GOVERNMENT ACQUISTION APPROACH. The documents below contain a description of the RFCBA requirements, technical data package, and a Contractor Capability Survey. The Survey allows Contractors to provide their company's capability. Attention Small Business Respondents who are interested in participation for this effort: 1. No set aside decision has been made; however, the USG will determine the final strategy after thorough analysis of the small business responses and other market research available, considering the demonstrated interest and capability. Please ensure that you provide a thorough response to each question. If you company does not currently possess the full capability required to fulfill the entire requirment, what teaming/partnership/joint venture/subctonracting arrangements do you have in place to fulfill the Government's needs? Provide evidence of this arrangement e.g. emails, letter, etcl. that demonstrate a united response to this Sources Sought is highly encouraged, but not required. The evidence should state the type of arrangement and the role each member will fulfill. If you are only interested in being a subcontractor to the future awardee, state the portion of the work your organization has capability of fulfilling. 2. Identify any areas of work that your organization believes should be broken out exclusively for Small Businesses. Both Large and Small Businesses are encouraged to participate in this Market Research. Joint Ventures or Teaming Arrangements are encouraged. Questions relative to this market survey should be addressed to Brandon Jones, Contracting Officer, AFLCMC/ESGK-R (brandon.jones.96@us.af.mil) and Elizabeth Fuller (elizabeth.fuller.2@us.af.mil), Lead System Engineer, and Robert Cowden (robert.cowden.ctr@us.af.mil). buyer: Consejo de Administración de la Empresa Provincial de Aguas de Córdoba S.A.
title: Spain – Water-treatment chemicals – Suministro de reactivos para la potabilización del agua en las Estaciones de Tratamiento de Aguas Potables (ETAP) que gestiona Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA mediante sistema dinámico de adquisición
description: Las diferentes Estaciones de Tratamiento de Agua Potable ETAP gestionadas por Aguas de Córdoba-EMPROACSA necesitan del suministro continuado de diferentes productos químicos a fin de garantizar el apropiado tratamiento y, por tanto, la salubridad del agua para poder cumplir con los parámetros exigidos por la normativa vigente para la potabilización del agua. Teniendo en cuenta la exhaustiva norma que regula la fabricación, transporte, descarga y dosificación de los productos empleados en la potabilización del agua de consumo humano y la necesidad permanente de suministro de tales productos, se hace necesaria la contratación de los mismos con empresas especializadas y que reúnan los requerimientos normativos exigidos para garantizar la salubridad del agua de consumo humano. La modalidad de contratación que se propone, a través de sistema dinámico de adquisición, nace de la necesidad de mejorar los tiempos de respuesta a determinadas necesidades de la organización.

title: DA01--Veterans Health Information Systems and Technology (VISTA) Blood Establishment Computer Software (VBECS) Operations and Maintenance Support II
description: VA is seeking sources that are able to provide full lifecycle sustainment and operational support, and any associated bug/fix development, and regulatory compliance services for the VA s existing Veterans Health Administration s VBECS, an FDA regulated Class II Medical Device Software product. The Contractor will be required to plan, manage, develop bug/fixes, test, deploy, maintain, document, and continuously monitor the VBECS system throughout the DevOps lifecycle. The Contractor will be required to maintain all system related documentation, ensuring accuracy, traceability, and compliance with FDA Quality System Regulations (21 CFR 820), ISO 13485:2016, and VA cybersecurity and privacy requirements. The Contractor will be required to support all activities required to maintain the VBECS s existing Authority to Operate, including preparation, validation, and submission of documentation within the SNOW Continuous Authorization and Monitoring environment, and continuous support for audits, assessments, and security reviews.

title: BPAs for Conference Rooms and Audio Visual Systems
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - Rock Island at Picatinny (ACC-RI-PICA), on behalf of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities and Development Command (DEVCOM) Armaments Center (AC) is issuing this Request for Quote (RFQ) to competitively select and establish multiple Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for the Repair, Replacement, Modification, and Modernization of Conference Rooms, Digital Workplaces, and Audio Visual (AV) Systems. The goal of this effort is to ensure that various collaboration spaces, office spaces, classrooms, conference areas, and Audio Video Teleconference (VTC) rooms remain state-of-the-art as the U.S. Army continues to digitize its data and operations.

title: Remedial Investigation (RI) and Optional Feasibility Study (FS) for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS), Former Fort Ord, Monterey County, California
description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. The Contractor must demonstrate technical capability conducting Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) bench-, pilot-, or full-scale efficacy evaluations targeting PFAS breakthrough and mass removal kinetics with preferred experience evaluating and optimizing existing pump-and-treat groundwater treatment plants (GWTPs) for PFAS removal across carbon be

description: ISBEE Set-Aside � Advanced Practice Provider Physician Assistant/Nurse Practitioner Services Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the HHS-adopted FAR Part 12, as supplemented by the attached solicitation documents. This announcement and its attachments constitute the solicitation. Quotations are requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation No. 75H70627Q00018 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), non-personal Advanced Practice Provider (APP) Physician Assistant (PA) and/or Nurse Practitioner (NP) healthcare services at Rosebud IHS Hospital, Rosebud, South Dakota. The Great Plains Area Indian Health Service (IHS) seeks a Contractor to provide qualified APP personnel sufficient to support two (2) full-time equivalent PA and/or NP positions providing outpatient primary care services at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic. Services include adult and pediatric primary care, chronic disease management, preventive and wellness services, acute outpatient care, authorized minor procedures, clinical documentation, referrals, care coordination, and quality-improvement activities. The Contractor shall furnish qualified licensed personnel, management, supervision, credentialing and privileging support, licensure and certification maintenance, professional liability insurance, staffing continuity, replacement personnel, and other Contractor-furnished resources necessary to perform the Performance Work Statement (PWS). This acquisition is set aside exclusively for Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs). The assigned NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, with a small business size standard of $34.0 million in average annual receipts. Quoters shall satisfy the applicable ISBEE eligibility and representation requirements and submit the completed IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form with their quotations. The anticipated award is a Firm-Fixed-Price, non-personal healthcare services purchase order using a Month-of-Service (MOS) pricing structure. One (1) MOS represents complete monthly performance of the required APP services, including qualified staffing equivalent to two (2) full-time PAs or NPs, scheduled outpatient clinic services, clinical documentation, care coordination, required training, and all other PWS requirements. The anticipated period of performance consists of a three (3)-month base period and three (3) option periods of three (3) months each, for a maximum potential period of performance of twelve (12) months. The anticipated base period is February 1, 2027, through April 30, 2027. Option-period dates will be specified in the resulting purchase order. Services will be performed at the Rosebud IHS Hospital Outpatient Department Clinic, 800 Hospital Drive, Rosebud, South Dakota 57570. Standard outpatient clinic hours are Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., excluding federal holidays, subject to the scheduling requirements identified in the PWS. Section F of the attached solicitation identifies the Contract Line Item Numbers (CLINs), service descriptions, quantities, units of measure, and performance periods. Quoters shall complete the price schedule with firm-fixed monthly MOS pricing for the base period and each option period. The Total Evaluated Price will include the base period and all three option periods. Award will be made to the responsible quoter whose quotation conforms to the solicitation requirements and represents the best value to the Government. Evaluation factors are Technical Capability and Management Approach, Past Performance, and Price. When combined, the non-price factors are significantly more important than Price. The Government intends to make a selection from initial quotations but reserves the right to request clarification, additional information, or revised quotations when determined appropriate. Questions must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) Central Standard Time (CST) on November 20, 2026. Quotations must be received no later than 12:00 p.m. (noon) CST on November 30, 2026. Submit questions and quotations electronically to David.Jones@ihs.gov, referencing RFQ No. 75H70627Q00018 � Rosebud APP Services in the email subject line. Quoters must have a valid Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), current System for Award Management (SAM) registration, and satisfy all applicable eligibility, responsibility, and exclusion requirements before award. Applicable solicitation provisions and contract clauses are identified in the attached Provisions and Clauses schedule. Prospective quoters are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Combined Synopsis/Solicitation, PWS and addendum, price schedule, quotation instructions, evaluation criteria, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, IHS Indian Economic Enterprise Representation form, and any amendments before submitting a quotation.
