description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. Granular Activated Carbon (GAC) Plant Efficacy: The Contractor must evaluate influent, mid-bed, and effluent monitoring campaigns across multiple Groundwater Treatment System (GWTS) facilities for short- and long-chain PFAS removal kinetics and plant optimization comingled with co-contaminants. title: BPA Conference Rooms and Audio Visual Systems
description: The U.S. Army Contracting Command - Rock Island at Picatinny (ACC-RI-PICA), on behalf of the U.S. Army Combat Capabilities and Development Command (DEVCOM) Armaments Center (AC) is issuing this Request for Quote (RFQ) to establish multiple Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for the Repair, Replacement, Modification, and Modernization of Conference Rooms, Digital Workplaces, and Audio Visual (AV) Systems. The goal of this effort is to ensure that various collaboration spaces, office spaces, classrooms, conference areas, and Video Teleconference (VTC) rooms remain state-of-the-art as the U.S. Army continues to digitize its data and operations. See attachments for details.

title: OCLC Software Renewal
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, Engineer Research and Development Center (ERDC), intends to issue an award to OCLC, Inc, 6565 Kilgour Place, Dublin, OG 43017-3395, a sole source basis utilizing Simplified Acquisition Procedures as outlined in RFO Part 12. The requirement is for software for a fully integrated library platform. This software is propriety to OCLC; OCLC, Inc is the sole source provider of the OCLC services. The OCLC electronic titles are as follows: WorldShare Management System SubscriptionEZproxy HostedOCLC Meridian. The NAICS code for this requirement is 513120 with the size standard of 1,000 employees. This notice is not a request for competitive quotes or proposals. A solicitation will not be issued; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation, which shall be considered by the agency. The information submitted must be provided in sufficient detail to demonstrate the vendors ability to fulfill this requirement. title: NONSKID FOR NAVAL SHIPS/VESSELS
description: The award resulting from this RFP will be an Indefinite Delivery, Indefinite Quantity (IDIQ) supply contract with prepriced ELINS for Nonskid Deck Covering Removal/Replacement onboard U.S. Navy Ships. Nonskid replacement shall be accomplished meeting the following Society for Protective Coatings (SSPC) surface preparation standards: SSPC-SP10/National Association of Corrosion Engineers International (NACE) 2 Near-White Blast Cleaning SSPC-SP 11, Power Tool Cleaning to Bare Metal SSPC-SP12 WJ-3/NACE 5, Surface Preparation and Cleaning of Steel and other Hard Materials by High and Ultra High Pressure Water Jetting Prior to Recoating. Nonskid application will be either MIL-PRF-24667 Type I or Type V roll-on nonskid, Type IV spray on nonskid, or Type XI peel and stick sections.

title: Forest Service Hand Thinning, MATOC North Rockies/Great Basin
description: Requirement includes a wide variety of non-merchantable vegetation management activities for the purpose of fuels reduction, prescribed burn unit preparation, stand improvement, or unit rehabilitation. Activities could include, but are not limited to, tree thinning, slashing, girdling, pruning, weed and release, release of browse species, slash treatment, hand piling, fuel break construction, Fireline construction, residual tree protection, duff mound removal, unit preparation work, rehabilitation, chipping and related services. Unit boundary/special protection area designation and/or traversing for or within these units may also be included in the activity.

title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

title: Pine Bluff Arsenal Testing, Lab and Engineering Services
description: The services provided include surface water, sediment, and fish tissue sampling in streams and large river systems, as well as ambient sediment toxicity testing to determine the effectiveness of corrective measures. Acute and chronic whole effluent toxicity testing is conducted for four NPDES permitted outfalls, with the capability to perform Toxicity Identification Evaluation and Toxicity Reduction Evaluation if needed. Additionally, statistical analysis is compiled and conducted for three RCRA Detection monitoring groundwater assessment reports (covering three regulated units) and twelve RCRA Corrective Action Closure sites annually. Maintenance and updating of the PBA-specific Geographic Information System database is also included. The services encompass preparing industrial stormwater permit renewals, Stormwater Pollution Prevention Plans, and stormwater sampling for three outfalls, as well as preparation of Construction SWPPPs and permits. Compliance assistance is provided for SPCC Plan development and review, RCRA Permit development and review, and CAA permit review, renewal, and reporting. The services also support a change of the State of Arkansas Water Quality Standards, Rule 2, for mercury at an NPDES outfall, and assist with contaminant transport investigations in Phillips Creek and the Arkansas River. *Amendment 0001 posted 12 November 2026 *Amendment 0002 posted 19 November 2026

title: 30 RS Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST)
description: This requirement is for procurement of services including providing personnel, services, and management support for the Mission Planning Software Tool (MPST) software. The service will provide timely remote and periodic on-site support to the 30RS for MPST. The service includes maintaining compatibility with upgrades to the RQ-170 Mission Planning System (MPS) software, hardware, and databases by utilizing improved and/or expanded intelligence products. It will also ensure the software accurately represents new and/or improved aircraft capabilities, correct errors and address limitations encountered during operational use. Provide software and database maintenance and support functions to the 30 RS for the Mission Planning Support Tools (MPST) and Advanced Framework for Simulation, Integration and Modeling (AFSIM). The contractor shall provide software programming support for MPST computer program and its integration with AFSIM. All individuals performing on-site on this PWS must have a current adjudicated background investigation and be eligible for access to Top Secret, SCI, SAP information and associated ACCMs. Contractor personnel shall be conversant in the computer programming skills to fully support MPST, the version of AFSIM used by the RQ-170 simulator, be familiar with RQ-170 aircraft survivability, capabilities, Blue/Gray/Red ground and airborne threat systems, and Suppressor modeling capabilities/architecture/function/programming. Suppressor model may contain Foreign Government Information. The contractor shall provide support in training in the use of the version of AFSIM currently being used by the RQ-170. Actual work performance location is the contractor facility with periodic on-site visits to Creech AFB, NV and other classified locations as determined by the government.

title: S207--BHVAHCS Building 65 Bat Mitigation Sources Sought
description: The Black Hills VA Healthcare System requires bat mitigation and exclusion services in accordance with the draft Statement of Work (SOW) below. This is a sources sought looking for vendors to perform the services per the SOW for market research purposes. No awards of a contract will be made from this announcement. If you are a vendor that can complete the work described in the SOW with competitive pricing, please send your contact and organization information with a descriptive proof of capability to: Jeffrey.Brown8@va.gov on or before November 30th, 2026. Only emailed responses will be considered. Additionally, please provide answers as appropriate to the following questions in the table below with your response to this sources sought. Failure to respond to the following questions may affect the acquisition strategy. Question # Questions Vendor Responses 1. Identify your organization's socio-economic category. � 2. State whether any of the requested services may be ordered against a government contract awarded to your organization (e.g Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), General Services Administration (GSA), etc.). � 3. State if subcontracting is contemplated for this requirement, what percentage of the work will be subcontracted and for what tasks. � � *If applicable, VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Veteran Owned Small-Businesses or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small-Businesses.* *If applicable, FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Small-Businesses.* Draft Statement of Work (SOW) Building 65 Bat Mitigation Black Hills VA Health Care System at Fort Meade, South Dakota General Intention: Contractor shall provide all supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project for the following services: Professional Bat abatement in attic of Building 65. Remove bat colonies, conduct bat proofing/exclusion, remove bat guano and insulation (sterilize as needed), sanitize the area, and reinstall insulation. Building 65 is a 2-story building with the attic above. General Requirements: Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, and incidentals necessary to accomplish work elements and requirements outlined in this Statement of Work (SOW). Where equipment, temporary installations, ingress/egress restrictions or any other consideration is necessary, signage in such areas shall be provided by Contractor. The Contractor shall confine all staging activities within the anticipated construction area. Contractor shall coordinate proposed staging areas with the facility representative for approval. The Contractor shall field verify all existing conditions, dimensions, and quantities prior to any work activities. Time and date to be coordinated with facility representative. Any work that is not addressed by the contract shall immediately be brought to the attention of the Contracting Officer. No out-of-scope or additional work shall be executed prior to modification of the contract by the Contracting Officer. Contractor shall remove all rubbish from the Fort Meade property and dispose off site following VA Specification 01 74 19 Construction Waste Management. Contractor shall record all quantities of materials removed from the Fort Meade property and turn into the facility representative monthly reports even if a null report. Contractor to perform all work during normal work hours, Monday through Friday 7:00 am to 4:30 pm Mountain Time except as coordinated with the facility representative for any activities that may need to occur outside of normal working hours at no additional cost to the Government. The requirements of this SOW supplement other related VA standards for construction, space and facility planning criteria, design guides, design manuals, specifications, and details, which remain in full force and effect. Specifically, all requirements of VA handbook 0730, NEC 517, NFPA Health Care Facilities Code for Branches, Security and Law Enforcement, Appendix B, (which covers physical security requirements for VA facilities), the VA fire Protection Design Manual (which covers all VA construction), and ICT standards on the TIL remain in effect. Work Elements: Which shall include and are not limited to: All supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project. Bat Exclusion: Bats need to be permanently excluded from roosting in the VA building 65 using non-lethal exclusion methods following Bat Conservation International (BCI), South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks recommendations, and comply with section 7 of the Endangered Species Act. The technique includes using one-way exit devices (industry preferred exclusion tubes VA approved), sealing points of entry, interior and exterior of the building, and preventing access to the building interior. Exclusion activities will be conducted when bats are not present if feasible; this timing will also ensure that activities occur before the Maternity and Roost season. Bat removal shall occur between February 1st, 2027 and April 15th, 2027. Exclusion may not be done when pups are too young to fly (June-August). Change to these timelines may be proposed and accepted after discussion and approval by the designated facility representative(s) and contracting officer. One-way exit devices through which bats can leave but cannot return are made from tube-type excluders which are placed at all active entry points. Exclusion tubes should have a diameter of two inches, a length of 10 inches with a smooth surface and should project no more than one-quarter inch into the opening. Once the tube has been secured over the hole, a piece of lightweight, clear plastic can be taped around the tubes outside end to further reduce the likelihood of bats reentering, though this may not be necessary. Multiple exclusion tubes may be required. Lightweight, flexible plastic netting with one-sixth-inch mesh or smaller can be used to form a one-way valve over openings on smooth surfaces of exterior walls or attic louvers. The one-way exit devices will remain in place for at least five to seven days. The devices will be removed after all bats have been confirmed to be excluded. Night observation and other means, may be needed when determining if bats are still entering or leaving the building. It must be confirmed by visual inspection or other that bats are no longer present. Sealing Exclusion Points Exclusion points will be sealed with OSI silicone sealant, caulk backing rod, hardware cloth or heavy-duty polypropylene mesh, flashing out required areas around roofline with proper metal for optimal coverage. If one-way exit devices have been used, sealing will be conducted after the five-to-seven days that the devices have been in place. Bats can enter buildings or living spaces through openings as small as 3/8 diameter. Focus points include but not limited to trim, soffits, chimneys, and dormers. All metal on the front roofs will be properly sealed and securely screwed down where required to prevent Bat re-entering the building. Appropriate screws designed for metal, equipped with washers to prevent leaks will be used, and sealed to prevent future water damage. Preventing Building Interior Access The building s interior will be inspected for small openings through which bats could enter. Bats can enter buildings or living spaces through openings as small as 3/8 diameter. All openings connecting potential roosting areas to living quarters need to be sealed. Methods not to be used for bat exclusion: Simply waiting for bats to fly out at night and then permanently sealing the entrances without the use of one-way exit devices. title: Remedial Investigation (RI) and Optional Feasibility Study (FS) for Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS)
description: This Sources Sought Notice is for Market Research ONLY to determine the availability, capability and interest of small business firms for a potential small business category type set-aside. NO AWARD will be made from this Sources Sought Notice. NO SOLICITATION, SPECIFICATIONS, OR DRAWINGS ARE AVAILABLE AT THIS TIME as this is solely for Market Research. Please do not request such documentation. Requests for any of this information will go unanswered. If the conditions at Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO)19.104-1(a) are met the contracting officer is required to set the acquisition aside for small business concerns. Accordingly, interested contractors who have the skill, capabilities, and workload capacity to complete the described project (either through self-performance and/or the managing of subcontractors) are invited to provide their capability statements to the point of contact listed below. All responses will be used to determine the appropriate acquisition strategy for a potential acquisition. The purpose of this notice is to obtain a snapshot of current market capabilities and gain knowledge of potential small business sources to include small business in the following socioeconomic categories: Certified HUB Zone; Woman-Owned Small Business (WOSB) and Serviced-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business (SDVOSB); Veteran Owned Small Business (VOSB) and 8(a) small business concerns to perform database updates to increase the capabilities, usability, and stability of currently existing applications. Other than small business are encouraged to express interest and submit capability statements as well. Contractors� capabilities will be reviewed solely for the purpose of determining an appropriate acquisition strategy to include whether this prospective action is appropriate to be set-aside for the small business community or should proceed as an unrestricted full and open acquisition. Other than small businesses are encouraged to respond to this NOTICE to provide a greater context of current market capabilities. However, per the Federal Acquisition Regulations, preference will be given to the small business categories as listed above. In determining the acquisition strategy, the Government must ensure there is adequate competition among the potential pool of available contractors. The Government intends to award a Firm Fixed Price order with a Period of Performance of five (5) years from date of award. An estimated solicitation date has not yet been determined. The NAICS Code is 562910, Environmental Remediation Services. The Size Standard in Number of Employees: 1,000 Employees. Product Service Code is B510. GENERAL SCOPE: Regulatory & Data Governance Regulatory Framework: This Base Realignment and Closure (BRAC) site is governed by the Comprehensive Environmental Response, Compensation, and Liability Act (CERCLA) in which the work must strictly adhere to the developed Per- and Polyfluoroalkyl Substances (PFAS) Remedial Investigation (RI) Quality Assurance Project Plan (QAPP) which utilizes the Uniform Federal Policy for Quality Assurance Project Plans (UFP-QAPP). The Contractor must transmit all documents and data via Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS). All actions are dictated by the Federal Facilities Agreement (FFA) with the regulatory community. The Contractor will anticipate significant comments on products generated for this effort and must present technically competent PFAS subject matter experts to address and resolve comments suitable for public consumption per EPA Risk Communication guidelines. The Contractor must demonstrate past experience executing CERCLA work under an active FFA alongside USACE, U.S. Army BRAC, U.S. EPA, California DTSC, and California Regional Water Quality Control Boards. Compliance Standards: All analyses must be conducted by Department of Defense (DoD) Environmental Laboratory Accreditation Program (ELAP)-accredited laboratories per DoD Quality Systems Manual (QSM) Table B-15 using DoD Module 3 data validation with Fort Ord Data Information Site (FODIS) upload and follow safety compliance per U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Engineer Manual (EM) 385-1-1 via an Accident Prevention Plan (APP) and Site Safety and Health Plan (SSHP). Technical & Key Personnel Qualifications: The Contractor must present an overview of qualified in-house staff or primary teaming partners (e.g., Professional Geologists/Hydrogeologists registered in California, Environmental Engineers with water treatment optimization expertise, Quality Assurance Chemists, and USACE EM 385-1-1 Certified Safety Professionals) and show the ability to identified commercial analytical laboratories possessing active DoD ELAP accreditation for PFAS analysis by LC/MS/MS compliant with DoD QSM criteria. 2. Field Characterization and Waste Management Subsurface Drilling: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must advance continuous soil borings advanced to groundwater (~100 feet below ground surface [bgs]) with discrete depth-interval profiling, conduct the installation of multi-cased wells per the Drilling, American Society for Testing and Materials (ASTM) D5092 construction, and conduct multi-aquifer development including shallow water table (~100 ft bgs), intermediate Upper 180-Foot Aquifer (~225 ft bgs), and deep Seaside Groundwater Basin (up to 500 ft bgs). Groundwater Monitoring: Per the PFAS RI QAPP, the Contractor must conduct baseline, seasonal, and base wide sampling rounds for plume delineation. The Contractor will be expected to have an advanced understanding of the areas subsurface hydrology given the Salinas-Valley Aquitard and its various discontinuities as influenced by local potable water and agricultural pumping variations and inform the Government on modifications to the existing MODFLOW model. The Contractor will be expected to operate and maintain existing multi-well port systems in monitoring wells. Strict PFAS Sampling Cross-Contamination Mitigation: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must adhere to strict avoidance of PFAS-containing field equipment, bailers, tubing, pumps, personal protective equipment (PPE), decontamination reagents, sunscreens, and vehicle materials and of documented PFAS Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and field blank / equipment rinsate validation programs. Investigation-Derived Waste (IDW) Protocols: The Contractor must be proficient at handling, containment, characterization, transportation, and disposal/destruction of PFAS-impacted drill cuttings, purge water, development water, and decontamination fluids in strict accordance with DoD and State of California regulations. 3. Specialized Comparative Studies HydraSleeve vs. Low-Flow: Per the PFAS RI QAPP the Contractor must demonstrate competency in the described field study assessing data quality, bias, and operational efficacy for PFAS passive sampling versus conventional purge techniques. The Contractor must demonstrate the ability to evaluate data comparability, turbidity impacts, sampling precision/accuracy, and relative bias for both short- and long-chain perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances, and past experience designing, executing, and reporting side-by-side comparative studies between passive sampling devices (specifically HydraSleeve) and conventional low-flow (minimal drawdown) purging/sampling techniques. The purpose of this procurement is to acquire SUREPOWER rechargeable lithium-ion battery packs and R Series WiFi Cards with Clock Sync, FIPS, for defibrillators used throughout the facility by Nursing staff. The batteries shall power the defibrillators used on crash carts. The R Series WiFi Cards shall provide network connectivity, with clock synchronization performed automatically through DXS after scheduled readiness tests. The anticipated requirement includes battery packs with 5.8 Ah capacity, high-density lithium-ion chemistry, a RunTime Indicator, automatic calibration readiness, and the ability to store use and maintenance history. The WiFi Cards shall meet the physical, wireless, security, environmental, certification, and operating-system requirements identified in the Statement of Work below. The contractor shall comply with the complete VA cybersecurity and privacy requirements included in the Statement of Work, including the requirements applicable to medical devices, specialized systems, wireless connectivity, FIPS-validated cryptography, patching, product integrity, incident reporting, and VA information-system access. STATEMENT OF WORK Description of Equipment Requested: SUREPOWER RECHARGEABLE LITHIUM-ION BATTERY PACK and R Series WiFi Card with Clock Sync, FIPS for defibrillators How Equipment Works: Batteries power the defibrillators to enable them to deliver a controlled electrical shock that depolarizes all heart muscle cells at once, stopping chaotic rhythms like ventricular fibrillation so the heart s natural pacemaker can restart a normal rhythm. This process is performed by devices such as AEDs, which analyze heart rhythms and shock only when needed. The R Series Wi Fi card enables network connectivity, while clock synchronization is performed automatically through DXS after scheduled readiness tests. Who Will Use This Equipment: Nursing staff Where it will be used: Throughout the facility Salient Characteristics: Battery Must have 5.8 Ah Capacity Must have High density lithium-ion chemistry Must have RunTime Indicator Must have Automatic calibration ready Must be able to store history of use and maintenance R Series Wifi Card Must have Standard: IEEE 802.11 a/b/g/n (single stream) Must have Interface: CompactFlash (CF) self contained CF to Wi Fi functionality (no host CPU load) Must have Bands: 2.4 GHz (2.412 2.462 GHz) & 5 GHz (5.180 5.825 GHz) Must have Data rates: Up to 65 Mbps (includes 54/58.5/52/39/26/19.5/13/6/5/5.5/2/1 Mbps) Must have Modulation: OFDM with BPSK, QPSK, 16QAM, 64QAM, CCK Must have Security: WPA/WPA2 PSK, WEP (64/128 bits), TKIP Must have Antenna: Embedded PCB printed, 1.30 dBi @ 2.4 GHz / 1.97 dBi @ 5 GHz Must have TX power: 9 dBm @ 802.11a, 14 dBm @ 802.11b, 11 dBm @ 802.11g, 10 dBm @ 802.11n, 8 dBm @ 802.11an Must have Sensitivity: 70 dBm @ 802.11a, 75 dBm @ 802.11b, 70 dBm @ 802.11g, 69 dBm @ 802.11n, 67 dBm @ 802.11an Must have Dimensions: 60.5 × 41.7 × 6.45 mm Must have Operating temp: 0 55 °C Must have Humidity: 20 % 95 % Must have Certifications: FCC, IC Must have OS support: Windows XP / 7 Additional Equipment Or Replacement Equipment (EE number): Replacement Equipment No EE#s - MVO Justification: Defibrillators are required for crash carts VA CYBERSECURITY AND PRIVACY LANGUAGE FOR INCLUSION IN ACQUISITIONS. title: S207--BHVAHCS Building 65 Bat Mitigation Sources Sought
description: The Black Hills VA Healthcare System requires bat mitigation and exclusion services in accordance with the draft Statement of Work (SOW) below. This is a sources sought looking for vendors to perform the services per the SOW for market research purposes. No awards of a contract will be made from this announcement. If you are a vendor that can complete the work described in the SOW with competitive pricing, please send your contact and organization information with a descriptive proof of capability to: Jeffrey.Brown8@va.gov on or before November 30th, 2026. Only emailed responses will be considered. Additionally, please provide answers as appropriate to the following questions in the table below with your response to this sources sought. Failure to respond to the following questions may affect the acquisition strategy. Question # Questions Vendor Responses 1. Identify your organization's socio-economic category. � 2. State whether any of the requested services may be ordered against a government contract awarded to your organization (e.g Federal Supply Schedule (FSS), General Services Administration (GSA), etc.). � 3. State if subcontracting is contemplated for this requirement, what percentage of the work will be subcontracted and for what tasks. � � *If applicable, VAAR 852.219-75 VA Notice of Limitations on Subcontracting Certificate of Compliance for Services and Construction, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Veteran Owned Small-Businesses or Service Disabled Veteran Owned Small-Businesses.* *If applicable, FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting, will apply to the potential solicitation if set-aside for Small-Businesses.* Draft Statement of Work (SOW) Building 65 Bat Mitigation Black Hills VA Health Care System at Fort Meade, South Dakota General Intention: Contractor shall provide all supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project for the following services: Professional Bat abatement in attic of Building 65. Remove bat colonies, conduct bat proofing/exclusion, remove bat guano and insulation (sterilize as needed), sanitize the area, and reinstall insulation. Building 65 is a 2-story building with the attic above. General Requirements: Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, materials, equipment, and incidentals necessary to accomplish work elements and requirements outlined in this Statement of Work (SOW). Where equipment, temporary installations, ingress/egress restrictions or any other consideration is necessary, signage in such areas shall be provided by Contractor. The Contractor shall confine all staging activities within the anticipated construction area. Contractor shall coordinate proposed staging areas with the facility representative for approval. The Contractor shall field verify all existing conditions, dimensions, and quantities prior to any work activities. Time and date to be coordinated with facility representative. Any work that is not addressed by the contract shall immediately be brought to the attention of the Contracting Officer. No out-of-scope or additional work shall be executed prior to modification of the contract by the Contracting Officer. Contractor shall remove all rubbish from the Fort Meade property and dispose off site following VA Specification 01 74 19 Construction Waste Management. Contractor shall record all quantities of materials removed from the Fort Meade property and turn into the facility representative monthly reports even if a null report. Contractor to perform all work during normal work hours, Monday through Friday 7:00 am to 4:30 pm Mountain Time except as coordinated with the facility representative for any activities that may need to occur outside of normal working hours at no additional cost to the Government. The requirements of this SOW supplement other related VA standards for construction, space and facility planning criteria, design guides, design manuals, specifications, and details, which remain in full force and effect. Specifically, all requirements of VA handbook 0730, NEC 517, NFPA Health Care Facilities Code for Branches, Security and Law Enforcement, Appendix B, (which covers physical security requirements for VA facilities), the VA fire Protection Design Manual (which covers all VA construction), and ICT standards on the TIL remain in effect. Work Elements: Which shall include and are not limited to: All supervision, tools, labor, materials, hardware, equipment, transportation, and incidentals necessary to complete a turnkey finished project. Bat Exclusion: Bats need to be permanently excluded from roosting in the VA building 65 using non-lethal exclusion methods following Bat Conservation International (BCI), South Dakota Game, Fish and Parks recommendations, and comply with section 7 of the Endangered Species Act. The technique includes using one-way exit devices (industry preferred exclusion tubes VA approved), sealing points of entry, interior and exterior of the building, and preventing access to the building interior. Exclusion activities will be conducted when bats are not present if feasible; this timing will also ensure that activities occur before the Maternity and Roost season. Bat removal shall occur between February 1st, 2027 and April 15th, 2027. Exclusion may not be done when pups are too young to fly (June-August). Change to these timelines may be proposed and accepted after discussion and approval by the designated facility representative(s) and contracting officer. One-way exit devices through which bats can leave but cannot return are made from tube-type excluders which are placed at all active entry points. Exclusion tubes should have a diameter of two inches, a length of 10 inches with a smooth surface and should project no more than one-quarter inch into the opening. Once the tube has been secured over the hole, a piece of lightweight, clear plastic can be taped around the tubes outside end to further reduce the likelihood of bats reentering, though this may not be necessary. Multiple exclusion tubes may be required. Lightweight, flexible plastic netting with one-sixth-inch mesh or smaller can be used to form a one-way valve over openings on smooth surfaces of exterior walls or attic louvers. The one-way exit devices will remain in place for at least five to seven days. The devices will be removed after all bats have been confirmed to be excluded. Night observation and other means, may be needed when determining if bats are still entering or leaving the building. It must be confirmed by visual inspection or other that bats are no longer present. Appropriate screws designed for metal, equipped with washers to prevent leaks will be used, and sealed to prevent future water damage. description: The previous RFI number 36C10B27Q0056 was corrupted in the system. This RFI replaces 36C10B27Q0056 and continues the previous RFI progress. VA is seeking sources that are able to provide full lifecycle sustainment and operational support, and any associated bug/fix development, and regulatory compliance services for the VA s existing Veterans Health Administration s VBECS, an FDA regulated Class II Medical Device Software product. title: MACH1_AOI_Military Working Dog Facility_ Vandenberg Space Force_LOE 1 and LOE 2
description: This Area of Interest (AOI) is published under the Modernized Agile Construction Horizons (MACH1) Umbrella Program Notice. All submissions must adhere to the procedures and guidelines outlined in the parent MACH1 framework document unless otherwise tailored herein. Any resulting agreement will be an Other Transaction Agreement (OTA) executed under the statutory authority of 10 U.S.C. � 2808a. The 772nd Enterprise Sourcing Squadron (772 ESS) is is executing a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) project to renovate existing military working dog (MWD) facilities and construct a new addition at Vandenberg Space Force Base (SFB), California. Under this agreement, the selected contractor will execute both the progressive design and physical construction to deliver a fully functional, code-compliant compound (Project Number: XUMU171121C). The current MWD kennel and admin facilities (Buildings 6444 and 6447) at Vandenberg SFB fail quarterly inspections and contain critical safety hazards that endanger military personnel and canine assets. Transitioning to a Progressive Design-Build (PDB) model is critical to eliminate traditional design-bid-build delays, rapidly deliver compliant spaces, and preserve the security mission of the 30th Space Wing. There are (2) two distinct lines of effort (LOEs) for this requirement: LOE 1 - Design & Planning (Design) and LOE 2 - Physical Construction. title: JBSA Lodging Revised Solicitation
description: Purpose of Amendment: The purpose of this amendment is to formally amend the subject solicitation as follows: Extension of Solicitation Due Date: The offer/quote submission deadline is hereby extended from 10 November 2026 to 30 November 2026, at 12:00 PM CDT. Acknowledgment and Acceptance of Amendment: Offerors must acknowledge receipt of this amendment prior to the revised hour and date specified for receipt of offers. Offerors shall acknowledge receipt by completing, signing, and returning the standard form (SF 1449 / SF 30). Returning the signed SF 1449 with the offerors submission constitutes full acceptance and acknowledgment of this amendment. Failure to acknowledge this amendment may result in rejection of the offer._____________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________________Solicitation Notice: Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Commercial Lodging BPA (FA301627Q0008)Scope of Work The 502d Contracting Squadron (502 CONS CL) at JBSA Lackland, Texas, is soliciting quotes to establish up to six (6) decentralized, firm-fixed-price Blanket Purchase Agreements (BPAs) for commercial off-base lodging accommodations. The selected contractors will provide clean, safe, and secure single and double occupancy lodging rooms within a 15-mile driving radius of JBSA-Lackland or JBSA-Fort Sam Houston to support transient military and civilian personnel. The agreements will cover a 12-month base period with four subsequent one-year option periods. All direct-billed government reservations must be processed as tax-exempt. Key Deadlines and Submission Details: Quote Submission Deadline: All electronic quotes must be fully submitted and received no later than 12:00 PM CST on November 10, 2026.Contractor Questions and Answers Deadline: Technical or administrative questions regarding this solicitation must be submitted using the designated Questions and Answers spreadsheet (Attachment 05) no later than 12:00 PM CST on October 28, 2026.Points of Contact for Submission: Submissions and questions must be sent via email directly to the primary Contract Specialist, SrA Autumn Mauran (autumn.mauran@us.af.mil), the Primary Contracting Officer, Doralo Fuller (doralo.fuller@us.af.mil), and CC Contracting Officer, Thomas Farrell (thomas.farrell.5@us.af.mil).Required Submission Documents: To be eligible for evaluation, contractors must electronically submit: completed and signed SF 1449 capability statement demonstrating active SAM.gov registration and small business status under NAICS code 721110 completed pricing lists (Attachment 03)FEMA fire safety and ADA compliance documentation completed Pre-Award Assessment Checklist (Attachment 04).

title: ISBEE Solicitation: Emergency Department Registered Nurse Services (Up to 8 RNs) � Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates IHS Hospital, Fort Yates, ND.
description: The Indian Health Service (IHS), Great Plains Area, is soliciting proposals for non-personal Emergency Department Registered Nurse services in support of the Standing Rock Service Unit, Fort Yates Hospital, Fort Yates, North Dakota, under Solicitation No. 75H70627R00002. The requirement is for up to eight (8) qualified Emergency Department Registered Nurse positions to support continuous 24-hour, 7-day-per-week Emergency Department operations. The anticipated contract type is Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP), commercial services, with one four (4)-month Base Period and fourteen (14) four-month Option Periods, for a total potential period of performance of sixty (60) months. This acquisition is set aside 100 percent for eligible Indian Small Business Economic Enterprises (ISBEEs) in accordance with the Buy Indian Act and applicable HHSAR requirements. The applicable NAICS code is 561320, Temporary Help Services, and the Product Service Code is Q401, Medical�Nursing. The Contractor will be responsible for providing qualified nursing personnel and all associated management, supervision, recruitment, credentialing, scheduling, replacement staffing, administrative support, and other resources necessary to perform the requirements of the Performance Work Statement. The requirement consists of up to eight (8) separately exercisable RN positions. The Base Period provides for up to eight (8) RN position CLINs, with the actual number of Base Period RN position CLINs awarded or funded identified in the resulting contract. During each Option Period, the Government may independently exercise from one (1) up to eight (8) RN position CLINs based on operational requirements and availability of funds. The Government is not obligated to award, fund, or exercise all eight RN positions, any particular RN position, or any Option Period. Pricing will be based on a common Firm-Fixed-Price RN Month of Service (RN/MOS) unit price for each performance period. The common RN/MOS unit price will apply uniformly to all RN positions within that performance period. The Total Evaluated Price will be based on the maximum potential requirement for the Base Period and all fourteen Option Periods; evaluation of all RN position CLINs and option prices does not obligate the Government to award, fund, or exercise all positions or options. Important Dates: Questions regarding the solicitation are due no later than November 13, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Proposals are due no later than November 30, 2026, at 12:00 p.m. Central Time. Award will be made using a Best Value Tradeoff process. Evaluation factors are Past Performance, Technical Approach, Management Approach, and Price. Past Performance, Technical Approach, and Management Approach, when combined, are more important than Price. Technical Approach and Management Approach will be evaluated using adjectival ratings of Outstanding, Good, Acceptable, Marginal, or Unacceptable. The Government may select a higher-priced proposal when the evaluated benefits of the non-price factors justify the associated price premium. Offerors are responsible for reviewing the complete solicitation package, including the Performance Work Statement, Price Schedule/Bid Sheet, applicable FAR/HHSAR provisions and clauses, Buy Indian Act/ISBEE representations, wage determination, and any amendments, prior to submitting an offer.

title: Department of War Pharmacy Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreement/Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program
description: The Department of War (DoW) is required by law (10 U.S.C. � 1074g) to establish an effective, efficient, integrated pharmacy benefits program for the Military Health System (MHS) which includes the purchase pharmaceutical agents. The law and implementing regulation (32 CFR Section 199.21) describe the process by which the DoW Pharmacy and Therapeutics (P&T) Committee will consider the relative clinical effectiveness and relative cost effectiveness of pharmaceutical agents in a therapeutic class in recommending the selection of agents for the DoW Uniform Formulary (UF) and, for cost sharing purposes, the classification of a pharmaceutical agent as generic, formulary, Basic Core Formulary (BCF), Extended Core Formulary (ECF), or non-formulary (NF). Prior to the scheduled P&T Committee meeting, a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for pharmaceutical agents within Drug Classes identified for placement on the UF has been issued to obtain quotes from industry. The Defense Health Agency may award Uniform Formulary Blanket Purchase Agreements (UF BPA) and the Uniform Formulary Additional Discount Program Agreements (UF ADP) based on the UF decision. This process is described in the attached RFQ. P&T COMMITTEE MEETING: The following February 2027 newly approved drugs will be reviewed: Atebrioz � Skeletal Muscle Relaxants and Combinations � Subclass: NA Emcitate � Thyroid and Antithyroid Agents � Subclass: NA Hibsago � Hepatitis B Agents � Subclass: NA Juvmo � Parkinsons Agents � Subclass: NA Zegfrovy � Lung Cancer � Subclass: EGFR+ NSCLC The RFQ, including UF BPA and UF ADP appendices, are attached herein. The instructions, important deadlines, and points of contact are in document, RFQ HT9402-27-Q-9102. Pre-quotation teleconference is on November 17, 2026. Details are stated in Part 2.4. Pre-Quotation Teleconference. Responses to the clinical questions in Part 3.4 shall be submitted via e-mail to the RFQ POC in Part 2.3.1., no later than the date stated in Part 2.3.2.

title: S222--Sources Sought - Hazardous Waste Removal/Disposal Northeast Ohio VA Healthcare System - Cleveland, OH
description: Hazardous Waste Pickup, Transportation, and Disposal Services, Cleveland VA Medical Center and Supported CBOCs CORRECTION NOTICE: This notice re-issues Sources Sought 36C25026Q0957, which closed on September 14, 2026. Question #4 of that notice referred to "Scrap Metal Recycling services" in error. The requirement is for hazardous waste services. Questions #4 through #7 below replace the original Question #4. Firms that responded to the original notice may revise and resubmit their responses, answering Questions #4 through #7, but are not required to. Firms that did not respond are encouraged to respond now. The Network Contracting Office (NCO 10) is seeking vendors to perform Hazardous Waste Pickup, Transportation, and Disposal Services at the Cleveland VA Medical Center and its supported Community Based Outpatient Clinics (CBOCs). This is a Sources Sought to identify capable sources and request industry feedback ONLY. This notice does not constitute a commitment by the Government. Interested parties are asked to answer the questions below AND submit a capability statement that clearly and convincingly demonstrates their ability to fulfill the requirement. The capability statement and answers to the questions below must be submitted electronically by email to Joshua.Kovar@VA.gov no later than 1:30 PM EST on November 30, 2026. As part of market research, this Sources Sought is intended to determine whether an adequate number of qualified, interested contractors exists that are capable of providing the requirement. Industry feedback is requested to ensure the VA has not created a "de facto sole source" requirement. The Government may use the responses for information and planning purposes. DRAFT SCOPE: The Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) is conducting market research to identify qualified sources capable of providing hazardous waste services at the Cleveland VA Medical Center and a number of CBOCs throughout Northeast, Central, and Northwest Ohio. The contractor will provide on-site support, packaging, transportation, and treatment and disposal of hazardous waste. The estimated hazardous waste volume is approximately 68,000 to 75,000 pounds per year. This estimate is provided solely for informational and market research purposes. The forthcoming solicitation will include a refined workload estimate based on updated facility data. The Government is proposing an Indefinite-Delivery, Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract with a five-year ordering period. The Government anticipates placing a task order each year to cover that year's requirements. QUESTIONS FOR INDUSTRY Question #1. Are you interested in providing a quote for this requirement? (Yes / No) Question #2. Please provide your company name, address, UEI, and a point of contact. State your business size under the NAICS code below and any SBA certifications (for example, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, EDWOSB, HUBZone, 8(a), small business). Veteran-owned firms should state their SBA VetCert status. Question #3. What is your current scope of operations and locations of service? Where do you currently work, and what is your maximum service area? Please state your ability to perform in Cleveland and in the CBOC locations across Northeast, Central, and Northwest Ohio. Question #4: Collection and packaging. Does your firm self-perform hazardous waste collection and on-site packaging with its own employees? (Yes / No) If no, what type of subcontractor would you use? Question #5: Transportation. Does your firm self-perform hazardous waste transportation with its own vehicles and drivers? (Yes / No) If no, what type of subcontractor would you use? Question #6: Treatment and disposal. Does your firm own or operate the permitted facility that treats or disposes of the hazardous waste? (Yes / No) If no, what type of subcontractor or facility would you use? Question #7: Licenses and permits. Does your firm hold, or have access through a subcontractor, the federal and state licenses and permits required to transport and dispose of hazardous waste in Ohio? (Yes / No) Answers to Questions #4 through #7 are for market research only and will help the Government understand industry practices and self-performance capabilities. CAPABILITY STATEMENT Please provide a capability statement that supports this requirement. Include relevant past performance, preferably hazardous waste services at a medical center or similar healthcare facility. NAICS AND PSC The applicable NAICS code is 562211, Hazardous Waste Treatment and Disposal, with a small business size standard of $47.0 million. The Product Service Code is S222, Housekeeping Waste Treatment/Storage. Businesses of all sizes are encouraged to respond. Each respondent must identify its business size in its capability statement and answer the questions above. DISCLAIMER This Sources Sought is only for the purpose of identifying potential sources as part of market research. No Request for Proposal (RFP), Request for Quote (RFQ), or Invitation for Bid (IFB) exists. Responses are not quotes, proposals, or bids on which the VA can issue a contract. This notice is issued for information and planning purposes only. The Government does not intend to award a contract based only on responses to this Sources Sought. Responses will not be returned. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding, and the VA will not pay for information received. Do not submit pricing information.

title: Yuma Proving Ground Job Order Contract (JOC)
description: SOURCES SOUGHT SYNOPSIS Job Order Contract for Yuma Proving Ground This is a Sources Sought Synopsis (SSS) ONLY. This notice is issued solely for information and planning purposes � it does not constitute a Request for Quotation (RFQ), Invitation for Bid (IFB), or Request for Proposal (RFP) or a promise to issue an RFQ, IFB or RFP in the future. This notice does not commit the U.S. Government to contract for any supply or service. Further, the U.S. Government is not seeking quotes, bids or proposals at this time and will not accept unsolicited proposals in response to this sources sought synopsis. The U.S. Government will not pay for any information or administrative costs incurred in response to this notice. Submittals will not be returned to the responder. Not responding to this notice does not preclude participation in any future RFQ, IFB, or RFP, if any is issued. If a solicitation is released, it will be synopsized on the Government wide Point of Entry (GPE). It is the responsibility of potential offerors to monitor the GPE for additional information pertaining to this requirement. The GPE is located at https://sam.gov. The United States (U.S.) Government desires to procure a Job Order Contract (JOC) at Yuma Proving Ground, on a small business set-aside basis, provided 2 or more qualified small businesses respond to this sources sought synopsis with information sufficient to support a set-aside. Be advised that the U.S. Government will not be able to set aside this requirement if two (2) or more small businesses do not respond with information to support the set-aside. We encourage all small businesses, in all socioeconomic categories (including, 8(a) Business Development Program, Small Disadvantage Business, Historically Underutilized Business Zone, Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned, Women-Owned Small Business concerns), to identify their capabilities in meeting the requirement at a fair market price. BACKGROUND: A continuing need is anticipated for a job order contract at Yuma Proving Ground. Attached you will find the draft Statement of Work (SOW). The Government contract for these services was previously performed under contract W91151-21-D-0012. The Period of Performance ended 1 August 2026. The contractor shall provide all personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, transportation, tools, materials, supervision, and other items and construction services as defined in this SOW. The NAICS code for the requirement is 236220, Commercial and Institutional Building Construction with a corresponding size standard of $45 million. If your company believes a different NAICS code would better fit this requirement, please tell us your suggested NAICS and why it would better fit this requirement. The Contractor shall provide all supervision, labor, personnel, equipment, materials, and supplies, with the exception of Government Furnished Property (GFP), to perform activities under this Job Order Contract. PURPOSE OF THIS SOURCES SOUGHT: To request information on capabilities of potential offerors to provide the services described herein. Electronic submissions only: Responses are due no later than 13:00pm CDT on 30 November 2026 to facilitate planning and ensure maximum consideration. The email attachments cannot exceed 9 megabytes (MB) due to the Government�s email system restrictions. DO NOT SEND ZIPPED files as the Government�s network will remove all zipped files. Interested businesses should provide a brief capability statement package (limited to no more than 30 pages, single spaced, and 12 font size minimum) demonstrating specific capability in reference to this requirement. The Government prefers that your firm submits its response in Microsoft Word, Adobe Acrobat, or a combination of the two and the document(s) must be searchable. Include: Whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). Email the capability package to: Marissa Joyner - Contract Specialist at email: Marissa.joyner.civ@army.mil and Andrew Graham - Contracting Officer at email: Andrew.s.graham6.civ@army.mil The email subject line should include: The Firm�s Name, �Response to the Sources Sought Synopsis for the JOC at Yuma Proving Ground, W5168W-26-R-A022". **Note: the location(s) and corresponding solicitation number that you are responding to must be identified on the subject line. In response to this sources sought, please provide: 1. A company�s profile must include: The name of the firm, point of contact, phone number, email address, number of employees, annual revenue history, CAGE code, and Unique Entity Identifier (UEI). number. Respondents must also indicate small business certification status, for example: Small Business (SB), Small Disadvantaged Business (SDB), 8(a), Economically Disadvantaged Woman Owned SB (EDWOSB), WOSB, HUBZone, or Service Disabled Veteran Owned SB (SDVOSB). 2. Respond to: What fundamental tasks you believe need to be performed to successfully accomplish the job order contract? In essence, what primary tasks should be used for determining minimum capability to provide these services? 3. Whether your firm is interested in competing for this requirement as a prime contractor. If you are subcontracting any of the services out, contemplating a Joint Venture, and/or creating a teaming arrangement, please provide the name of these companies and what work they will be performing, if available. Please provide your company�s specific experience in job order contracts and providing comparable services. Ensure the information is in sufficiently detailed regarding previous experience in managing job order contracts (indicate whether the experience has been as a prime contractor or subcontractor) on similar requirements (include the services provided, the number of facilities involved, and any other relevant information you deem applicable). If applicable, please provide the same experience information from any subcontracts, Joint Venture, and/or teaming partners you may propose with. 4. What percentage of work will be performed by the small business prime contractor and all similarly situated entity subcontractors? Note: In accordance with FAR 52.219-14 Limitations on Subcontracting (Oct 2022) and Class Deviation 2021-O0008, Revision 1 - Limitations on Subcontracting for Small Business (Feb 2023), for general construction under NAICS 236220, prime contractor and similarly situated subcontractors must perform at least 15% of the cost of the contract, excluding the cost of materials. 5. Type(s)/certifications(s) of proposed subcontractors (for example, SDB, 8(a), HUBZone, SDVOSB, or WOSB). 6. Information on the financial capacity of your business to meet financial obligations (i.e. payroll, payment of subcontractors, etc.). 7. How the Army can best structure these contract requirements to facilitate competition by and among small business concerns. 8. Identify any condition or action that may have the effect of unnecessarily restricting competition with respect to this acquisition. Please contact the MICC Advocate for Competition, Scott Kukes at email: scott.d.kukes.civ@army.mil or 210-466-3015, if you believe that this action is unreasonably restricting competition. Include the subject of the acquisition, this announcement, and the MICC POC information from the notice on https://sam.gov. Provide the specific aspects that unreasonably restrict competition and the rationale for such conclusion.

description: Sources Sought Notice Sources Sought Notice Page 4 of 4 Sources Sought Notice *= Required Field Sources Sought Notice Page 1 of 4 Network Contracting Office 8 (NCO 8) for the Orlando VA Healthcare System is conducting market research to gain knowledge of potential qualified sources to perform Annual Cathodic Protection Inspection & Testing for the Orlando VA Healthcare System (OVAHCS), located at 13800 Veterans Way, Orlando, FL 32827. This is a market research/sources sought synopsis only, (not a pre-solicitation notices pursuant to FAR Part 5). This Sources Sought Notice (SSN) is for planning/information purposes only and shall not be construed as a commitment or a promise of a contract by the Government. This is not a solicitation. This notice does not constitute a Request for Bid, Request for Quote or Request for Proposal, nor does it restrict the Government as to the ultimate acquisition approach. The Government will not reimburse respondents for any costs incurred in preparation of a response to this notice. The purpose of this notice is for market research purposes only and to make appropriate acquisition decisions to gain knowledge of potential qualified businesses and their Small Business Administration (SBA) size classification in relation to North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code 541380 Testing Laboratories and Services with a size standard of $19.0 Million. Project scope: The Contractor shall perform annual inspecting, testing and evaluation of the existing galvanic cathodic protection (CP) system serving the underground coated steel steam and condensate pipelines at the Orlando VA Medical Center, Lake Nona Campus. The purpose of this testing is to verify continued compliance with NACE cathodic protection criteria, ensure electrical isolation integrity, check anode performance, and document all monitoring results in a comprehensive annual report. Large and small businesses are encouraged to participate in this survey. This survey is to determine the capability of potential sources and the availability of commercial sources and services pursuant to FAR Part 10. title: Airport BAER Weed Treatment
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Quotations are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 127EAT27Q0004 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Airport BAER Weed Survey and Treatment. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 115310 The small business size standard is $11.5M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Statement of Requirement The purpose of this project is to procure services to survey and treat target non-native plants in areas affected by the 2024 Airport Fire. The contractor will survey and treat up to 200 acres of areas impacted by the Airport Fire on the Trabuco Ranger District of the Cleveland National Forest. Survey and treatment areas will include: trails, meadow areas, Forest road sides, riparian areas, chaparral, and campgrounds. Surveys and treatments will prioritize known non-native weed infestations that were impacted by the fire and fire suppression activities. Period of Performance for this requirement is date of award through 30 September 2027. Quotes shall be submitted to megan.acord@usda.gov and are due no later than November 30, 2026 at 12:00 PM MT. title: HANGAR 140 RENOVATIONS AT NAVAL AIR STATON (NAS) JACKSONVILLE (JAX), JACKSONVILLE, FLORIDA
description: The H140 Renovations project scope encompasses the entire 111,000 SF facility, including the Administration, Shops, and Maintenance wings (O1 and O2 spaces) as well as the Organizational Hangar (OH space). The O spaces will include space reconfiguration and replacement of finishes, ceiling systems, lighting and plumbing fixtures. Work also includes replacement of the sliding steel hangar bay doors. Building envelope work will replace the high-bay clerestory windows with high-efficiency thermal windows and provide repair or replacement of walls, cladding, windows, doors. Roofing systems over the hangar high bay, and administration wings will be replaced, while exterior envelope rehabilitation will address hazardous material removal, concrete and masonry repair, and sealing and recoating of surfaces. Replaced building envelope components will be designed to achieve hurricane resistance, Anti-Terrorism Force Protection compliance, and weather-tight performance, but do not entail modifications to the structure. Also included to replace three bridge cranes, two 5 Ton and one 2 Ton. The anticipated performance period for this contract will be 945 calendar days. The magnitude of construction is between $50,000,000 and $100,000,000. The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) Code for this solicitation is 236220 � Commercial and Institutional Building Construction, PSC Z2JZ - Repair or Alteration of Miscellaneous Buildings with a Small Business Size Standard of $45 million (M). Under the FAR guidelines, the prime contractor must have the capability to perform at least 15 percent of the contract work with its own employees. The anticipated award date is Fourth Quarter FY 27. Interested sources are invited to respond to this sources sought announcement. Capability Statements consisting of appropriate documentation will be accepted providing it contains ALL the information required below (items 1-6). Complete submission package shall not exceed 4 pages. The information which must be contained in your response is as follows: 1) Contractor Information: Name and address of company, point of contact with phone number and email address. 2) Type of Business: Identify the company�s business size and socio-economic status (HUBZone, 8(a), SDVOSB, WOSB, etc.), if applicable for NAICS Code 236220 applicable to this sources sought. If your firm is claiming HUBZone or 8(a) status, provide a copy of your SBA certification. 3) Bond Capacity: Information must include surety�s name, point of contact, telephone number, email address, and the bonding capacity of at least $50 Million per project, and the maximum aggregate bonding. 4) System for Award Management (SAM): Evidence of registration in the SAM, including Cage Code and Entity Identifier (formerly DUNS Number). 5) Interest: Indicate if a solicitation is issued will your firm/company be submitting a proposal: _____ Yes ______No. 6.) Existing Contract Vehicles your firm may have (GWAC, FSS, MACC, MATOC, etc.) available for this work. 7.) Experience Submission Requirements: Responders shall provide a minimum of two (2) to a maximum of three (3) projects including contract numbers, project titles, dollar amounts, project completion dates, performance ratings, and evidence of specific capabilities listed below: Demonstrate Prime Contractor experience constructing or repairing an industrial facility that was self-performed. Projects submitted for the Offeror shall be valued at approximately $50 million or greater, similar in size, scope and complexity to the proposed hangar repairs and completed and accredited/certified within the past five (5) years of the date of issuance of this announcement. Provide a brief description including completion date and final contract value. If they are not approximately equal to the requested dollar value, identify the dollar value and explain in no more than one paragraph why we should consider the project. The response to this sources sought is not expected to be a proposal, but rather short statements regarding the company�s ability to demonstrate existing-or-developed expertise and experience in relation to the areas specified herein. Submission of Capabilities statement is not a prerequisite to any potential future offerings, but participation will assist the Government in tailoring requirements to be consistent with industry capabilities. After completing its analysis, the Government will determine whether to limit competition among 8(a), HubZone, SDVOSB, VOSB, WOSB, and/or Small Business firms or to proceed with issuing an unrestricted solicitation, inviting full and open competition. Please respond to this announcement no later than 30 November 2026, NLT 2:00 PM Eastern Standard Time via email to Delcheia Turner, Delcheia.l.turner.civ@us.navy.mil and Aimee Johnson, aimee.n.johnson2.civ@us.navy.mil. Responses that do not meet all requirements or are not submitted within the allotted time will not be considered. Respondents will not be notified of the results of the evaluation.

This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; proposals are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. Solicitation number 70Z03826RJ0000001 is issued as a Request for Proposal (RFP) using the procedures of FAR part 12 in conjunction with FAR part 15. This solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect as of November 28, 2025, IAW the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO). All responsible sources may submit a quotation which shall be considered by the agency. It is anticipated that one (1) Indefinite Delivery Requirements type contract with firm-fixed pricing (FFP), consisting of a one (1) year base period and, if exercised, two (2) one (1) year option periods will be awarded as a result of this synopsis/solicitation. All parts shall have clear traceability to the Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM), Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation, (Cage Code 78286). Traceability means a clear, complete, documented, and auditable paper trail which traces each step from the OEM to its current location. Sikorsky Aircraft Corporation is the OEM and the only approved source of supply. All overhauls must be approved in accordance with �Attachment 3, �Statement of Work � 70Z03826RJ0000001�. Newly manufactured commercial items will only be procured from sources able to provide a certificate of airworthiness, FAA 8130 (preferred) or equivalent European Aviation Safety Agency (EASA) Certification, or a certificate of conformance and traceability to the OEM. The Federal Aviation Regulation, Part 21, outlines certification procedures. The contractor shall furnish a Certificate of Conformance (COC) in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) clause 52.246-15. description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in FAR Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Solicitation number 127EAT27Q0004 is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ) for Airport BAER Weed Survey and Treatment. This acquisition is set-aside for small business concerns. The applicable North American Industry Classification Standard Code is 115310 The small business size standard is $11.5M This acquisition is a Total Small Business Set-Aside. All responsible sources may submit a quotation which will be considered by the agency. Statement of Requirement The purpose of this project is to procure services to survey and treat target non-native plants in areas affected by the 2024 Airport Fire. The contractor will survey and treat up to 200 acres of areas impacted by the Airport Fire on the Trabuco Ranger District of the Cleveland National Forest. Survey and treatment areas will include: trails, meadow areas, Forest road sides, riparian areas, chaparral, and campgrounds.
